parts.title: hnz as an importable block: Python API (PyO3/maturin wheel), Windows packaging, concurrency model, OpenVINO loading, compat checks, C ABI + HTTP
parts.design:
## 0. What gets shipped
- **Code**: one wheel, `hnz-<ver>-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl`. It is pure Rust behind a thin Python shim and runs on Python 3.10–3.14. It has a single dependency, `openvino>=2025.1,<2027`, and uses only its DLLs: the package never runs `import openvino`.
- **Data**: one read-only block directory, `hn-YYYY-MM.hnz\`, made of 7 or fewer files. It holds both the data and the models, because the LM belongs to the format. Size: about 5.0–5.7 GB for the compact profile and 10.4 GB for the fast profile.
- **Other access paths**: the same Rust core also builds `hnz.exe` (CLI plus a multithreaded HTTP server) and `hnz.dll` + `hnz.h` (a JSON-in/JSON-out C ABI) for languages other than Python.
- **Rollout**: the Python layer can ship first on today's fast segments. Compact-profile pieces plug in later behind `block.json.profile` without changing the API.

## 1. Crate and package layout
```
hnz/ (cargo workspace; keeps .cargo/config.toml rustflags target-cpu=x86-64-v3)
  core/  crate `hnz` (rlib)   today's src/ minus main.rs; new: api.rs (facade), block.rs, service/{lm,embed,admission}.rs
         features: default=["runtime"]; runtime=[openvino,tokenizers]; build=[arrow,parquet]
         (gates item::read_parquet, segment::build, lm::store::write); http=[tiny_http]
  cli/   crate `hnz-cli`, bin `hnz` (clap)        -> hnz{build,http}
  py/    crate `hnz-py`, cdylib `_hnz` (PyO3)     -> hnz{runtime,http}; maturin mixed project python/hnz/
  capi/  crate `hnz-capi`, cdylib `hnz.dll` + cbindgen hnz.h -> hnz{runtime}
```
**Why a separate crate instead of a `python` feature:**
- PyO3 stays out of the CLI and C-ABI builds.
- The core remains a plain rlib, and maturin builds exactly one cdylib.
- Build-only dependencies (arrow/parquet, clap) never end up in the wheel. Today they are unconditional dependencies of the single `hnz` package, so they compile into anything that uses the lib.

**Release profile:** `lto="fat"`, `codegen-units=1`, `panic="unwind"`, `strip="symbols"`.
- `panic="unwind"` is required because every FFI entry uses `catch_unwind`. With `abort`, a panic would kill the host Python process.
- LM bit-exactness does not depend on these settings. Rust never contracts float operations into FMA, there is no fast-math, and the LM path makes no libm calls (only BM25 uses log2/powf/ln). A canary self-test proves this at open (§10).

## 2. Python API (exact)
```python
# hnz  (python/hnz/__init__.py + _hnz.pyi; Python >= 3.10, Windows x86-64-v3)
__version__: str; FORMAT_VERSION: tuple[int,int]  # newest block format readable, e.g. (2,0)
MATH_VERSIONS: tuple[int,...]                       # LM numeric versions decodable, e.g. (2,)
Size = int | str          # bytes, "2GB" (=2e9), "2GiB" (=2**31), "512MB"
DateLike = str | int | datetime.date | datetime.datetime
Kind = Literal["story","comment","job","poll","pollopt"]

def open(path, *, ram: Size = "2GB", threads: int|None = None, device: Literal["auto","cpu","gpu"] = "auto",
         max_concurrent: int|None = None, queue_timeout: float|None = 60.0,
         preload: Literal["models","all","none"] = "models", require_semantic: bool = True,
         ov_libs: str|PathLike|None = None, cache_dir: str|PathLike|None = None, cache_disk: Size = "512MB",
         self_test: bool = True) -> Archive
def inspect(path) -> dict          # block.json + compat report + RAM hints; loads no model
def serve(archive: Archive, host="127.0.0.1", port=8088, threads=8) -> None   # blocking, GIL released

class Archive:                      # thread-safe; one per process; not picklable
    path: str; profile: Literal["fast","compact"]; docs: int; time_range: tuple[int,int]; closed: bool
    def search(self, query: str = "", *, k: int = 10, offset: int = 0,
               since: DateLike|None = None, until: DateLike|None = None,
               types: Kind|Iterable[Kind]|None = None, author: str|None = None,
               mode: Literal["hybrid","vector","keyword"] = "hybrid",
               text: Literal["none","title","snippet","full"] = "snippet",
               include_dead: bool = False, thread_context: bool = True,
               rerank: Literal["auto","exact","off"] = "auto", candidates: int|None = None,
               timeout: float|None = None, cancel: CancelToken|None = None,
               explain: bool = False, raw: bool = False,
               w_bm25: float = 0.15, c_bm25: float = 20.0) -> SearchResult | dict
    async def asearch(self, query: str = "", **kw) -> SearchResult | dict
    def get(self, id: int, *, text: Literal["title","snippet","full"] = "full",
            timeout: float|None = None, raw: bool = False) -> Item | dict | None
    def get_many(self, ids: Sequence[int], **same) -> list[Item | dict | None]   # one LM batch
    async def aget(self, id: int, **kw) -> Item | dict | None
    def embed(self, texts: Sequence[str], *, kind: Literal["query","document"] = "query") -> list[list[float]]
    def stats(self) -> dict
    def close(self, timeout: float|None = 30.0) -> None     # also __enter__/__exit__, atexit
class CancelToken: cancel(); cancelled: bool

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Hit: rank:int; id:int; kind:str; by:str; time:int; date:str; points:int; title:str|None; url:str|None;
           text:str|None; html:str|None; partial:bool; tier:Literal["zstd","lm"]; parent_id:int|None;
           story_id:int|None; story_title:str|None; score:float; vscore:float; bm25:float; link:str
           # explain=True adds: v_bin, v_exact, rank_before_rerank
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SearchResult: query:str; hits:list[Hit]; timings_ms:dict[str,float]; warnings:list[str]; profile:str
                    # __iter__/__len__ over hits; timings keys: queue, embed, search, rerank, fetch, total
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Item: id:int; kind:str; by:str; time:int; date:str; title:str; url:str; html:str; text:str; points:int;
            descendants:int; parent_id:int|None; poll:int|None; parts:list[int]; dead:bool; deleted:bool;
            tier:str; partial:bool      # lossless except the HN `kids` order, which is not stored
```
`Hit` mirrors `engine::ResultItem` field for field. `raw=True` returns plain dicts with exactly the JSON schema used by HTTP and the C ABI, so FastAPI can return them directly.

**Basic use:**
```python
import hnz
with hnz.open(r"D:\hn\hn-2026-10.hnz", ram="4GB", threads=8) as hn:
    r = hn.search("how do I deal with burnout", k=10, since="2015", until="2018-06", types="comment")
    for h in r: print(h.rank, h.date, h.by, h.story_title, (h.text or "")[:120])
    it = hn.get(9700000)                                   # it.html = original HN HTML, lossless
    jobs = hn.search(types="job", since="2024", text="title")  # no query: newest first
    kw = hn.search("tokio", mode="keyword", author="steveklabnik")
    print(r.timings_ms, hn.stats()["memory"])
```
**FastAPI, single process with threads (requirement 7):**
```python
hn = hnz.open(r"D:\hn\hn-2026-10.hnz", ram="6GB", threads=8, max_concurrent=2)
app = FastAPI()
@app.get("/search")
def search(q: str = "", k: int = Query(10, ge=1, le=100), since: str|None = None, until: str|None = None,
           type: list[str]|None = Query(None), by: str|None = None, mode: str = "hybrid", full: bool = False):
    try: return hn.search(q, k=k, since=since, until=until, types=type, author=by, mode=mode,
                          text="full" if full else "snippet", timeout=20, raw=True)
    except hnz.QueryError as e: raise HTTPException(400, str(e))
    except hnz.BusyError: raise HTTPException(503, "busy")
    except hnz.TimeoutError: raise HTTPException(504, "timeout")
@app.get("/item/{id}")
def item(id: int):
    it = hn.get(id, raw=True)
    if it is None: raise HTTPException(404)
    return it
@app.on_event("shutdown")
def _close(): hn.close()
# uvicorn app:app --workers 1   (sync endpoints run in Starlette's threadpool; hnz releases the GIL)
# async: `return await hn.asearch(q, raw=True)` = asyncio.to_thread + CancelToken fired on CancelledError
```

## 3. Semantics
**Dates (`since` / `until`).**
- Strings `"2015"`, `"2015-06"`, `"2015-06-01"` mean inclusive periods, parsed by `dates::parse` exactly as in the CLI (`until="2018-06"` includes all of June).
- `int` (epoch seconds) and `datetime` values are exact instants with `since <= t < until`; naive datetimes are treated as UTC.
- `date` objects mean whole days, inclusive.

**Types and author.** `types` takes one kind or an iterable of kinds; job, poll and pollopt take the exact metadata scan, as today. `author` is an exact, case-sensitive match on `by`.

**`text` modes.**
- `none`: metadata only. LM-tier titles need decoding, so they come back as None.
- `title`: title and url. This costs about 15–30 LM tokens per cold record.
- `snippet`: title, url and the first 64 body tokens (`SNIPPET_TOKENS`).
- `full`: lossless HTML plus plain text.

**Rerank.** `rerank="auto"` is off in the fast profile. In the compact profile it means an exact re-embed of `candidates` (default 100). `"off"` in the compact profile is fast but measured at P@10 0.151 instead of 0.221 at 192 bits.

**Limits.** `k + offset <= 500` (`MAX_K`).

**Timeouts and cancellation.** `timeout` and `cancel` abort queued and active LM/embedder work and free its memory.

**Warnings.** The `warnings` list reports, among other things:
- a keyword-only search on frequent terms in the compact profile, which is approximate;
- a corrupt record, which is reported and dropped rather than failing the whole search.

**What `ram` covers.** It is a hard cap on memory that hnz owns or pins:
- model weights and tokenizers;
- OpenVINO compiled models, including the iGPU's shared memory;
- LM KV slots and logits;
- resident indexes;
- caches;
- per-query working memory, reserved when the query is admitted.

OS file-cache pages behind read-only mmaps are not counted, because Windows can drop them. Python result objects are not counted either. `open()` raises `BudgetError(required, budget)` when the mandatory part does not fit. `stats()["memory"]` reports the per-component breakdown alongside the process's measured `PrivateUsage` and working set (`GetProcessMemoryInfo`).

**Thread-safety contract.**
- All `Archive` methods may be called concurrently from any number of threads, and all of them release the GIL while working.
- Admission is a FIFO semaphore of `max_concurrent` (default 4 in the fast profile, 2 in the compact one). A query that waits longer than `queue_timeout` raises `BusyError`.
- `close()` waits for in-flight calls up to `timeout`, then cancels them. Afterwards every call raises `ClosedError` and every mmap is dropped, so the snapshot directory can be deleted or replaced (Windows locks mapped files).
- Hot swap: `new = hnz.open(new_dir)`, switch the reference, then `old.close()`.

## 4. Errors
The hierarchy is defined in `python/hnz/errors.py` so it can use multiple inheritance. Rust raises these classes, looked up once and cached in a once-cell.
```
Error(Exception)
 ├ BlockNotFoundError(Error, FileNotFoundError)
 ├ IncompatibleBlockError(Error)        .what .block .supported .hint  (format/MATH_VERSION/model id/OV min)
 ├ CorruptBlockError(Error)             .component .detail  (hash, rec_check byte, canary mismatch, truncation)
 ├ RuntimeMissingError(Error, ImportError)  OpenVINO missing/too old/conflicting, CPU lacks AVX2
 ├ BudgetError(Error, MemoryError)      .required .budget (bytes)
 ├ QueryError(Error, ValueError)        bad k/offset/dates/types/mode/text
 ├ BusyError(Error)                     admission wait > queue_timeout
 ├ TimeoutError(Error, builtins.TimeoutError)   work cancelled at the deadline
 ├ CancelledError(Error)
 ├ ClosedError(Error, RuntimeError)
 └ InternalError(Error, RuntimeError)   Rust panic caught; the archive stays usable
```
PyO3's default `PanicException` derives from `BaseException`, so it would slip past `except Exception` in web frameworks. Every entry point therefore converts panics to `InternalError` explicitly.

## 5. How Python maps onto the Rust engine
- **Core facade** (`hnz::api`): `Archive(Arc<Inner>)` is `Send + Sync` and wraps:
  - today's `Engine` (Arc'd);
  - the Block;
  - the Budget;
  - `EmbedService`, `LmService` and `Admission`;
  - one `rayon::ThreadPool` per Archive (`search` runs inside `pool.install`);
  - the typed error type `HnzError` (internals keep `anyhow`).
- **Call path:**
  1. The Python shim normalizes arguments into a dict. It converts dates to epoch values or keeps strings, and expands `types` to a list.
  2. `_hnz.Archive.search(req: dict, cancel)` deserializes it with `depythonize::<SearchRequest>`; serde errors raise `QueryError`.
  3. Rust takes a read lock, clones the Arc, and drops the lock.
  4. `py.detach(move || guard(|| a.search(&req, &tok)))` runs. It is called `allow_threads` before PyO3 0.26. All Rust work, including waiting in the LM and embedder queues, runs without the GIL.
  5. `pythonize(&SearchResponse)` builds the result (GIL held).
  6. The shim wraps the result in dataclasses, unless `raw=True`.
- **`guard()`** is `catch_unwind` plus `HnzError`-to-exception mapping.
- **Binding type:** `#[pyclass(frozen)] struct PyArchive { inner: parking_lot::RwLock<Option<api::Archive>> }`. Making it `frozen` means there is no borrow flag, and concurrent `&self` calls are fine.
- **Closing:** `close()` takes the archive out under the write lock, then calls `py.detach(|| a.shutdown(t))`.
  - It must detach, because in-flight calls need the GIL to finish converting their results. Waiting while holding the GIL would deadlock.
  - `Drop` also shuts down without touching Python, and an `atexit` hook closes any archives still open.
- **Worker threads never call Python.** Logs use the `log` crate. Per-request warnings go into the response; global events are emitted on the calling thread at `open`, `stats` and `close`, so pyo3-log never needs the GIL from a worker.

## 7. Sharing the LM decoder and the embedders across concurrent queries
```
Python threads --detach--> Admission(sem max_concurrent, per-query reservation 2-30 MB; up to ~1 GB worst case at k=500 → capped)
   ├ EmbedService.query  : CPU int8 IR, 2 InferRequests in a lock-free queue, NUM_STREAMS=2, INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS=4 (~20 ms)
   ├ Engine.search       : per-Archive rayon pool (ms)
   ├ compact: LmService.submit(prefix jobs, prio=Interactive, deadline, cancel)
   ├ compact: EmbedService.docs(batch)  → GPU batcher (static buckets 16x128, 16x256; 2 async requests)
   ├ fuse / rerank → top-k
   └ LmService.submit(title/snippet/full for top-k, prio=Fetch) → fetch → response
```
**`LmService`** is one scheduler thread, generalizing `LmCodec::decode_stream`. Each step:
1. Drop cancelled or expired sequences and release their KV.
2. Admit queued sequences by (priority, deadline) for as long as `budget.try_reserve(kv_bytes(ntok_cap))` succeeds.
   - `ntok` is in the record header before decoding starts, so the reservation is exact once `KvCache` reserves exactly instead of doubling.
   - Each token costs 24 KiB, so a 128-token prefix needs 3 MiB.
3. Call `Batch::step` over the active slots of every query, so the weights are streamed once per step for everybody.
4. Arithmetic-decode one token per row and complete finished jobs through oneshot channels.

Further rules:
- Priority order: Interactive (rerank prefixes, snippets, titles) > Fetch (full text, `get`) > Background.
- Option: keep the KV and decoder state of the top-k after rerank, so `text="full"` continues from token 128 instead of re-decoding.
- A panic inside a step fails the jobs in that step with `InternalError`, resets the slots, and the scheduler keeps running.
- Capacity is shared: about 2,300 tokens/s in total (measured). A cold compact query needs about 6–8k tokens, so throughput is roughly 0.3–0.4 cold compact queries/s however many run concurrently. Extra concurrency only adds queueing; RAM helps through caches (exact-embedding cache, decoded-prefix cache).

**`EmbedService`:**
- Queries always run on the CPU (lowest latency).
- Document re-embedding uses a single batcher thread. It mixes documents from concurrent queries into full buckets.
  - Device: GPU if `device` is `auto` or `gpu` and the GPU compiles; otherwise CPU with dynamic shape. The NPU is excluded: measured, it fails to compile (E10).
  - iGPU memory is system RAM, so it is charged to the budget.
- Re-embedding must reproduce `embed_month.py` exactly. That means: strip tags, `html.unescape`, collapse whitespace, use the prompt `title: X | text: Y`, and cap at 256 tokens. The E27 rerank simulation used exactly those build-time vectors.

## 8. Finding and loading the OpenVINO runtime
**Search order.**
1. The Python shim tries, in order:
   - `ov_libs=`;
   - `HNZ_OV_LIBS`;
   - `importlib.util.find_spec("openvino").submodule_search_locations[0]\libs` (this does not import openvino or its 100+ MB of bindings);
   - `OPENVINO_INSTALL_DIR` / `INTEL_OPENVINO_DIR` + `runtime\bin\intel64\Release`;
   - an optional vendored `<block>\runtime\`.
2. If nothing is found:
   - `require_semantic=True` raises `RuntimeMissingError`;
   - `require_semantic=False` opens in keyword/listing-only mode.

**Loading (Rust, once per process via OnceLock):**
1. `libloading::os::windows::Library::load_with_flags(dir\openvino_c.dll, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS)`. This resolves openvino.dll and tbb12.dll from the same directory. The handle is leaked and never unloaded, because TBB threads stay alive.
2. `openvino_sys::library::load_from(dir)` binds the symbols; openvino-sys itself rejects versions older than 2025.1.
3. `ov_get_openvino_version()` must match the dist-info version of the chosen directory. If user code already loaded a different `openvino.dll`, Windows binds to that one by name, so hnz refuses with `RuntimeMissingError`.

No PATH edits, no `add_dll_directory`. Plugins load from the same directory; the GPU plugin needs `OpenCL.dll` from the Intel driver. CPU properties (`INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS`, `NUM_STREAMS`, `PERFORMANCE_HINT`) are set with `Core::set_property` before `compile_model`, because openvino 0.11 passes no per-compile properties.

## 9. Models inside the block
```
hn-2026-10.hnz/        (read-only; attrib +R)
  block.json           format, versions, ids/hashes, segment table, sizes, RAM hints, canaries
  data.hnzp            all segments packed; each component = (offset,len) slice of ONE read-only mmap
  models/lm.hnzlm      71.7 MB, mmapped and used in place (today: std::fs::read into a Vec)
  models/lm.tok.zst    3.56 MB json -> ~0.8 MB
  models/embed.xml/.bin  int8 IR, dynamic [batch, seq], ~3.5 + 272 MB; plain files so OpenVINO mmaps the weights
  models/embed.tok.zst 32.2 MB json -> ~7 MB
```
- **LM:** `LmModel::from_bytes(Bytes)`, where `Bytes` is an `Arc<Mmap>` plus a range. The id stays `fnv_full`.
- **Tokenizers:** zstd-decompress, then `Tokenizer::from_bytes`.
- **Embedder:** `Core::read_model_from_file`. Loading from memory is avoided: openvino 0.11's safe API can only build the weights tensor by copying (`Tensor::new`), which would cost an extra 272 MB of private memory.
- **Segment readers:** they take `&[u8]` slices instead of opening ~15 files per segment.
- **Dev mode:** `open("out", models="models")` still reads today's layout.

## 10. Versioning and compatibility
`block.json` holds:
- `format {major, minor, min_reader}`;
- `built_with` (hnz version, git hash, rustc);
- `profile`;
- `lm {file, model_id, math_version, tokenizer_xxh3}`;
- `embed {model_id(xxh3 of bin), dims:768, query_prompt, doc_prompt, max_tokens, ov_min, doc_bits}`;
- `pack {bytes, xxh3}`;
- `segments[]` (id range, time range, n_docs, tier, vec_bits, component slices);
- `ram_hints` (mandatory bytes per component, measured by the builder);
- `canaries` (about 4 record ids with a hash of their decoded bytes).

**Checks at `open()`:**
- Format: `min_reader <= FORMAT_VERSION`, otherwise `IncompatibleBlockError` naming the hnz version needed.
- Math version: `lm.math_version` must be in `MATH_VERSIONS`. The library keeps the decoders for every math version it ever shipped (v1 and v2 differ only in the order of attention sums), so a library upgrade never makes an old snapshot unreadable.
- LM id: `lm.model_id` must equal the hash of the loaded bytes and every segment's `lm.json`.
- Embedder: size plus xxh3 of the xml (full hash of the bin only with `inspect(verify=True)`); `ov_min`.
- Self-test (`self_test=True`, about 0.1–0.3 s): decode the canaries fully and compare their hashes. A mismatch raises `IncompatibleBlockError("LM decode mismatch ...")`.

## 11. Building the wheel on this machine (stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu + WinLibs)
- **`py/Cargo.toml`:** `hnz = {path="../core", default-features=false, features=["runtime","http"]}`, `pyo3 = {version="0.26", features=["extension-module","abi3-py310","generate-import-lib"]}`, plus `pythonize` and `pyo3-log` at the matching versions, and `parking_lot`.
- **`pyproject.toml`:** build backend `maturin>=1.7,<2`; `[tool.maturin] python-source="python"`, `module-name="hnz._hnz"`, `strip=true`; `requires-python=">=3.10"`; `dependencies=["openvino>=2025.1,<2027"]`; extra `server=[fastapi,uvicorn]`; script `hnz=hnz.__main__:main`.
- **Build commands:**
  - `cd hnz\py && maturin build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -o dist`. `generate-import-lib` creates `python3.dll`'s import library with MinGW `dlltool`, and the workspace `.cargo/config.toml` adds x86-64-v3.
  - `maturin develop --release` for local testing.
  - Alternative: MSVC Build Tools plus the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` target, the most-tested path for wheels. LM bits are identical either way.
- **CPU guard.** The `.pyd` is compiled for x86-64-v3 (VEX-encoded instructions can appear anywhere), so the shim checks first: `ctypes.windll.kernel32.IsProcessorFeaturePresent(40)` (AVX2), with `39` (AVX) used to tell "unknown on an old OS" apart from "absent". Escape hatch: `HNZ_SKIP_CPU_CHECK=1`.
- **Acceptance checks:**
  - `objdump -p _hnz.pyd` imports only system DLLs and `python3.dll`. `libgcc_s_seh-1`, `libwinpthread-1` and `libstdc++` must not appear (tokenizers already builds with `default-features=false`, so there is no esaxx C++); if they do, link statically.
  - pytest on the 3-month sample block:
    - `get` is lossless against Parquet;
    - ranking matches `hnz search --json`;
    - 32 threads × 20 queries give the same results as running them sequentially;
    - a Python counter thread keeps advancing during a long search (proves the GIL is released);
    - timeout and cancel free the LM slots;
    - the budget holds (`stats().memory.used <= ram`; `PrivateUsage` within ram plus about 150 MB of slack);
    - a tampered `block.json` raises the right error;
    - a bad `ov_libs` raises `RuntimeMissingError`;
    - after `close()` the block directory can be deleted;
    - `HNZ_KERNEL=scalar|avx2` gives identical bytes.

## 12. Other languages
- **C ABI** (`hnz.dll` + `hnz.h`): JSON in and out, with the same schema as `raw=True`. The handle is thread-safe. Strings are freed with `hnz_free`, never the caller's CRT `free`. Panics are caught at the boundary. Exact signatures are in the interfaces section.
- **HTTP:**
  - `hnz.exe serve` (no Python needed: the exe, the block and the OpenVINO DLL folder are enough) or `python -m hnz serve` (via `hnz.serve`).
  - tiny_http with N worker threads calling `server.recv()`, replacing today's single-threaded loop.
  - Endpoints: `GET /search` (today's parameters plus aliases), `POST /search` (JSON), `GET /item/{id}`, `POST /items`, `GET /stats`, `GET /health`.
  - Binds 127.0.0.1 by default and has no authentication.
parts.risks:
1. **GNU toolchain wheel.** Generating the PyO3 import library with dlltool may fail, or MinGW runtime DLLs (libgcc_s_seh, libwinpthread) may end up as dynamic imports and break `import hnz` with "DLL load failed".
   - Mitigation: an objdump acceptance check, static linking, or switching to MSVC Build Tools (the standard path for wheels).
2. **LM bit-exactness across builds** (fat LTO vs thin, gnu vs msvc, a newer rustc). In theory nothing changes: there is no fast-math, no implicit FMA and no libm in the LM.
   - Mitigation: canary self-test at open, CI test vectors per MATH_VERSION and per kernel (scalar/avx2/vnni).
   - Rules: never introduce `mul_add` or fast-math; never delete an old MATH_VERSION decoder.
3. **Oversubscription** between the LM spin pool, rayon and OpenVINO/TBB threads. It is measured: 17.3 s vs 1.03 s per LM batch (E17). Concurrent queries make it more likely.
   - Mitigation: a single LM submitter thread, a per-Archive rayon pool, OpenVINO thread caps, and one `threads` budget.
4. **Throughput.** Compact cold throughput is bound by the LM (~0.3–0.4 q/s), so concurrency only adds queueing. Users may expect thread-level scaling.
   - Mitigation: `max_concurrent=2` by default, `BusyError` with `queue_timeout`, and budgeted caches for exact embeddings and decoded prefixes.
5. **Budget accuracy.** iGPU allocations may not appear in process PrivateUsage, so GPU memory could be under-counted. OS file-cache pages behind mmaps are not counted by definition, which may surprise someone who reads "2 GB" strictly.
   - Mitigation: read OpenVINO GPU memory statistics, document the definition, and consider a `ram_strict` mode later.
6. **OpenVINO DLL conflicts.** If the user's code loads another openvino.dll version first, Windows binds to it by name.
   - Mitigation: the version check (refuse with `RuntimeMissingError`); recommend one OpenVINO per process. openvino-sys 0.11 also refuses runtimes older than 2025.1.
7. **Rerank fidelity.** The E27 "no loss" result used the build-time vectors: the full text up to 256 Gemma tokens, preprocessed with Python's `html.unescape` and regex. Re-embedding a decoded prefix of 128 LM tokens, or using slightly different preprocessing in Rust, is not validated.
   - Mitigation: port `clean()` exactly and validate rerank P@10 on the 900-query set before relying on it.
8. **Existing code hazards for a shared library:**
   - `set_var("PATH")` (unsound with concurrent threads);
   - L1 locks held across L2 and zstd I/O (serializes fetches);
   - mutex poisoning causing endless panics;
   - L2 written into the block directory;
   - panics surfacing as BaseException.
   All must be fixed before shipping (§6).
9. **Windows file locking.** Mapped block files cannot be replaced or deleted while an Archive is open. Snapshot swaps must open the new directory and then close the old one, and `close()` must really drop every Arc'd mmap, including ones held by queued jobs.
10. **AVX2 detection.** `IsProcessorFeaturePresent(40)` may give a false negative on older Windows builds; this is fine on the Windows 11 target. A wrong positive would crash Python with an illegal instruction, so the check runs in the shim before the `.pyd` is loaded.
11. **Tokenizer memory.** The Gemma tokenizer (262k vocab) could take a large, unmeasured share of a 2 GB budget. Authors stored as `Vec<String>` cost about 4× more than a blob.
12. **Large responses.** Results for k=500 with `text="full"` produce MB-sized Python objects, which sit outside the budget.

parts.title: hnz RAM budget manager + caches (compact profile, Windows x86-64, Python-importable block)
parts.design:
## 0. Decisions at a glance
1. **What `ram_budget` caps.** It caps resident memory (the Windows working set) that belongs to hnz: the tokenizer, OpenVINO CPU/iGPU allocations, LM weights, resident index parts, the LM KV pool and step scratch, embedder activations, per-query scratch and the caches.
   - The default is `scope="hnz"`. With `scope="process"` the cap covers the whole process working set; the host's usage is measured at open, and caches shrink if the host grows.
   - Two things are not capped. One is commit charge: OpenVINO commits about 0.5 GB at `Core()` and never touches it (measured). The other is the Windows standby file cache, which the system owns and can reclaim; `io="direct"` bypasses it.
2. **How it is enforced.**
   - Every component makes a reservation in one central `MemBudget`.
   - Opaque native parts (the tokenizer and OpenVINO) are measured from process counters at open, and that measurement becomes their reservation.
   - A counting global allocator and a 1 Hz working-set sample only verify the numbers and correct drift.
   - There is no `SetProcessWorkingSetSizeEx` hard cap, because it pages out Python and OpenVINO private pages. There is no Job-object commit cap by default.
3. **No mmap for data that should not stay resident.**
   - Resident parts are private, aligned copies, counted exactly, and filled by a background loader after open.
   - Cold parts use positional reads into per-query scratch.
   - Non-resident vector codes are read as large sequential streams.
   - mmap exists only in an opt-in `share="mmap"` mode for several processes sharing the archive.
4. **LM working memory is one decode service.** It is built from `decode_stream` (continuous batching) and uses a paged KV pool of 32-token pages (768 KiB each). Each record is admitted by its exact token count, which is already in its header (`ntok`). The arithmetic runs in the same order, so output stays bit-identical and `MATH_VERSION` does not change.
5. **Caches hold the results of expensive work** (LM decoding and re-embedding):
   - resumable prefix token ids;
   - int8 exact embeddings;
   - story titles;
   - query results.

   They live in a byte-exact S3-FIFO cache on a log-structured VirtualAlloc arena, so eviction really gives memory back to the OS.
6. **The planner fills the budget by value per byte**, in this order:
   - models;
   - the FST (BM25 term dictionary);
   - working pools;
   - the iGPU embedder, at 4 GB and above;
   - vector codes, newest segments first;
   - BM25 norms and postings;
   - the warm cache (elastic);
   - metadata and author columns.
7. **Can part of the archive be decompressed into RAM at load? Yes for the indexes, no for the text.**
   - Indexes load in about 1 s.
   - LM-compressed text cannot be bulk-decompressed: it costs about 30 ms of CPU per document, or about 120k documents per hour on 8 threads. Text therefore fills RAM gradually, on demand and through idle pre-warming.
   - At every budget level, cold queries stay limited by decoding: about 3–4.5 s for a top-100 rerank.
   - What RAM buys is warm latency (0.6 s down to 0.15 s), warm capacity and concurrency.
8. **The minimum workable budget is about 1.0 GB** with today's models, and about 0.7 GB after slimming the embedder and tokenizer. The disk cache is off by default. It can be switched to `temp` (deleted on close, zero bytes at rest) or to a persistent sidecar file.

## 1. Windows facts that drive the design (measured on this machine)
Probe setup: the project `.venv` Python with OpenVINO 2026.4.1, the same runtime `embed.rs` loads through `HNZ_OV_LIBS`. Memory read with psutil and the PDH counter "GPU Process Memory".

| Step | Change in working set (WS) | Other |
|---|---|---|
| gemma2_tokenizer.json (HF tokenizers) | +66 MB steady | peak WS 357 MB while parsing (0.76 s) |
| pythia tokenizer | +10 MB | only needed to encode, never to decode |
| import openvino + `Core()` | +32 MB | private commit +502 MB, never touched |
| read_model, int8 IR b1_s64 | +29 MB | the .bin file is mapped |
| compile on CPU | +354 MB (private WS +211 MB) | 1.9 s |
| infer request + first infer / a 2nd request | +9 MB / ≈0 MB | 18 ms per query (36 ms the first time) |
| fp16 IR b32_s128 on CPU | ≈ +1.6 GB | 2.05 s per 32×128 batch (15.6 docs/s) |
| fp16 IR b32_s128 on iGPU | +1.38 GB (GPU shared 1.25 GB) | 189 ms per 32×128 batch (169 docs/s); only 0.32 GB returned after the model is dropped |
| int8 IR b1_s64 on iGPU | +0.90 GB (GPU shared 0.65 GB) | 7.5 ms median, 11.2 ms p90 per query |
| int8 IR b1_s64 reshaped to 16×128 | fails | the static shape is baked in |

What follows from these measurements:
- **iGPU memory counts.** It is system RAM and appears in the process working set, so working-set accounting already includes it.
- **The device is chosen once per process.** The OpenVINO GPU plugin does not return memory when a model is dropped.
- **Commit is far larger than resident memory.** Commit is never capped by default. If a Job-object limit is wanted anyway, it must be at least budget + 0.6 GB.
- **The tokenizer has a parse peak.** Models must load before any index or cache memory is reserved, or the tokenizer must ship in a compact binary format.
- **Mapped files are invisible to budgeting.** Their pages count in WorkingSetSize (what psutil `rss` and the Task Manager "Working set" column show) but not in private bytes, and the OS trims them lazily. They cannot be accounted, so they are not used for cold data.

Counters used:
- `GetProcessMemoryInfo(PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX2)` for WorkingSetSize, PrivateWorkingSetSize and PrivateUsage.
- `IDXGIAdapter3::QueryVideoMemoryInfo(NON_LOCAL)` for the per-process iGPU share (reporting only).
- `CreateMemoryResourceNotification(LowMemoryResourceNotification)`: when the system is low on memory, caches shrink by 25 %.

## 2. Inventory (all HN, 49.3 M documents, compact profile)
Tags: M = measured, C = computed from code or file sizes, E = estimate.

| Class | Item | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed | Gemma tokenizer | 66 MB (M) |
| | Query embedder, CPU int8 | 424 MB (M) |
| | iGPU embedder (replaces the CPU one at ≥ 4 GB) | 0.9–1.4 GB (M); about 1.1 GB with dynamic shapes (E) |
| | LM weights (.hnzlm, scales, rowsum, rope) | 73 MB (C) |
| | Small structures: lm.idx 12.3 MB, meta.idx 0.8 MB, vec.has 6.2 MB, flags 49.3 MB at 1 B/doc (24.7 MB at 4 bits), packed author table 13–25 MB (E) | 70–100 MB |
| | Threads and allocator slack | 40–100 MB (E) |
| Index | Vector codes, 192 / 256 bits | 1.18 / 1.58 GB (C) |
| | FST of rare terms (the `fst` crate needs it contiguous) | 0.03–0.3 GB (E): one global FST about 0.03, yearly segments about 0.1, monthly about 0.3 |
| | BM25 norms; rare-term postings | 49 MB (C); 0.3–0.35 GB (E) |
| | meta.bin compressed; author column (u32); fully decoded columns | 0.28 GB; 0.20 GB; 1.0–1.2 GB (C) |
| | lm.bin text | 2.84 GB, never resident: decoding costs far more than the read |
| Working | KV cache 24 KiB per token; logits 196.5 KiB per active sequence per step | see §4 |
| | Re-embed activations on CPU (batch ≤ 8, ≤ 160 tokens) | 60–120 MB (E) |
| | Per-query scratch | 4–16 MB (C/E) |
| Cache | One fully warmed document: prefix ids 120–160 B (E) + int8 embedding 772 B (C) + index ≈ 20 B | ≈ 0.95 KB; prefix only ≈ 0.17 KB |

## 3. Residency and I/O
A `Blob` type replaces every `Mmap` today (vec.bin, bm25.*, meta.bin, lm.bin). It has three forms:

- **`Resident`.** A private, 4 KiB-aligned VirtualAlloc buffer, filled by a background loader.
  - Reads are sequential 8 MB requests with `SEQUENTIAL_SCAN`, plus `NO_BUFFERING` when `io="direct"`.
  - Counted exactly.
  - Optional `pin_indexes`: VirtualLock after raising the soft minimum working set, so system memory pressure cannot trim the vector codes.
- **`Disk`.** Positional reads.
  - On Windows, a synchronous file handle serializes its I/O, so there is one handle per I/O worker (or one overlapped handle) to reach queue depth 16–32.
  - `RANDOM_ACCESS` is set for lm.bin, postings and meta.
  - About 200 candidate records (in coalesced 32-record groups) take about 2–5 ms on this NVMe (E).
- **`Mapped`.** Only in opt-in `share="mmap"` mode, prefetched with `PrefetchVirtualMemory` and reserved at its full size.

Other rules:
- **Non-resident vector codes go through a "scan train".** One sequential stream (a ring of 4 × 8 MB, reserved once) is shared by all queries waiting for a scan. 1.18–1.58 GB at 2–5 GB/s takes about 0.3–0.8 s (E).
- **The FST is always resident** as `fst::Map<AlignedBuf>`, unless the format specialist adopts a blocked term dictionary for the 1 GB level.
- **Buffered I/O lets the OS standby cache use free RAM** to speed up cold reads; that memory is never charged to the process. Cold-latency benchmarks must therefore use `io="direct"` or flush the standby list first.

## 4. LM working memory
**Current behaviour (from `lm/model.rs` and `lm/store.rs`):**
- The KV cache stores, per layer, K transposed as `[hidden][cap]` in f32 and V as `[pos][hidden]` in f32. That is 6 layers × (512 + 512) × 4 B = **24,576 B per token**.
- Today's growth doubles K from 32 and grows V as a Vec, which gives up to 2× slack plus a copy at each doubling:

  | Sequence | Memory per sequence |
  |---|---|
  | Snippet | 3 MiB |
  | Prefix of 160 tokens | 6 MiB |
  | Full record of 2,000 tokens | 48 MiB (≈ 72 MiB during the last doubling) |

- `Batch::step` allocates 196.5 KiB of logits per active sequence per step.
- `sample` allocates a 393 KiB `cum` Vec per task per step.

**New `KvPool`.** A fixed array of 768 KiB pages; each page holds 32 tokens (per layer, K^T `[512][32]` and V `[32][512]`).
- The attention loop already scores keys in blocks of 32. Each key's sum runs in d order and V accumulates in j order.
- Walking pages therefore keeps every float operation in the same order, and the output is bit-identical. This must be proved with `hnz verify` on the three sample segments.
- A record needs `ceil((min(ntok, cap) + 1) / 32)` pages, known from its header before decoding starts.

**`DecodeService`.** One scheduler thread, and the only caller of the spin pool.
- **Requests:** a document key, the record bytes, what is wanted (`TitleOnly`, `Body(n)` or `Full`) and an optional resume point.
- **Priorities:** Interactive, then Fetch, then Background.
- **Admission:** a record starts only when a slot and its pages are free. The head of the queue keeps its reservation, so a 2,000-token record (63 pages) is never starved.
- **Scratch:** step scratch is preallocated.
- **Parking:**
  - When interactive work arrives, background sequences are parked.
  - Their token ids and decoder state `{code, range, pos}` are saved as a `PrefixEntry`, and their pages are freed.
  - To resume, the saved ids are run through `prefill`, which gives identical logits by construction.

**Pool size per level:**

| Budget | Slots | Pages | KV memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 GB | 16 | 96 | 72 MiB |
| 2 GB | 32 | 160 | 120 MiB |
| 4 GB | 32 | 224 | 168 MiB |
| 10 GB | 64 | 384 | 288 MiB |

Each level adds 4–20 MB of step scratch.

**Throughput:**
- 2,300 tokens/s at 64 slots (M).
- 10 snippets from E26 work out to about 2,700 tokens/s (C), so 16–32 slots lose little on short prefixes (E).

**Option for the LM specialist** (decide before the full rebuild): f16 K/V under `MATH_VERSION 3` would halve KV memory.

## 5. Embedder memory
**CPU, the default below 4 GB.**
- **Model:** one int8 IR exported with dynamic shapes (batch ≤ 8, sequence ≤ 160). This export is required because the current int8 IR is fixed at 1×64.
- **Sharing:** one compiled model serves both queries (one infer request per in-flight query, ≈ 0 MB each) and the re-embedding batcher.
- **Memory:** about 424 MB plus 60–120 MB of activations.
- **Cores:** `INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS` and `SCHEDULING_CORE_TYPE` are set so OpenVINO does not take the LM's cores.
- **Never** run the fp16 IR on CPU (1.6 GB, measured).

**iGPU, chosen automatically at ≥ 4 GB when an Intel GPU is present.**
- **Model:** one dynamic-shape GPU model for queries and documents, about 1.1 GB.
- **Speed:**
  - queries: 7.5 ms, against 18 ms on CPU;
  - documents: 169 per second at 128 tokens (M), about 250 per second with length buckets (E).
- **CPU embedder:** not loaded unless the budget is ≥ 8 GB, where it is kept only to isolate query latency.
- **Batching:** ≤ 8 documents (about 50 ms), so a query embedding never waits long.

**Overlap with decoding.** Re-embedding runs alongside decoding: each candidate is embedded as soon as its prefix finishes.
- On CPU the int8 model does about 50 documents/s (E), which keeps pace with about 33 decoded prefixes/s but competes for cores. That adds about 0.5–1 s to a cold query (E).
- On the iGPU this cost is hidden.

## 6. Caches
Every entry is keyed by `DocKey = seg << 32 | doc`.
- **`PrefixEntry`:**
  - Token ids as u16 (with zstd: 120–160 B per document, E), the decoder state `DecState` and a `complete` flag.
  - Text is rebuilt by concatenating `token_bytes`, which takes microseconds, and the entry can be resumed to the full text.
  - It covers snippets, rerank prefixes, on-the-fly BM25 and the full text of short records, which are most of HN.
- **`EmbI8`:** 768 int8 values plus an f32 scale (772 B). The key also carries the embed-configuration id.
- **`Title`:** the root story's title, about 50–80 B.
- **`QueryEntry`:** a separate small LRU. It maps (query, filters, build_id) to the query vector and the reranked list of up to 200 results, so repeated queries and later pages return in under 10 ms.

**Structure.** 16 shards. Each shard is an **S3-FIFO** (small queue 10 %, main queue 90 %, ghost queue of keys) over a **log-structured arena** of 256 KiB VirtualAlloc chunks.
- **Eviction:** the oldest chunk is scanned; entries used again are moved forward, the rest are dropped, and the chunk is released with `VirtualFree`.
- **Exact size:** cache size is exactly the committed chunks + the index (≈ 20 B per entry) + the ghost queue (8 B per key), and the working set really drops.
- **Claw-back:** the cache implements `Evictable`.
- **Split:**
  - with the iGPU: 70 % prefixes / 30 % embeddings, because re-embedding a miss is cheap;
  - on CPU only: 40 / 60.
- **What it replaces:** the current L1 and titles caches in `engine.rs`, which are `HashMap`s capped at 20,000 entries, cleared completely when full, and not counted in bytes.

## 7. Planner, and what each level buys
`plan()` steps (each step can be filled fully or partly, and it runs again on `set_ram_budget`):
1. **Floor:** tokenizer + embedder (measured) + LM + small structures + slack + FST + minimum pools. If the budget is below this, open fails with `BudgetTooSmall` and the breakdown.
2. **Device:** iGPU when the budget is ≥ about 3.5–4 GB.
3. **Pools:** slots, pages and `max_inflight` grow with the budget.
4. **Vector codes:** resident newest segments first. A partly resident index scans its resident part in milliseconds and streams the rest.
5. **BM25:** norms, then postings, then the title and query caches.
6. **Warm cache:** gets whatever remains. From 8 GB up, meta.bin and the author column are also kept resident.

Memory plan per level (GB):

| | 1 GB | 2 GB | 4 GB | 10 GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer / LM / small structures / slack | .07 / .075 / .07 / .04 | .07 / .075 / .10 / .05 | .07 / .075 / .10 / .06 | .07 / .075 / .10 / .10 |
| Embedder | CPU .42 + .06 | CPU .42 + .12 | iGPU ≈ 1.1 | iGPU 1.1 + CPU .42 |
| KV pool + step scratch | .09 (16 slots) | .14 (32 slots) | .19 (32 slots) | .32 (64 slots) |
| Query tickets | .03 (2 queries) | .05 (3) | .06 (4) | .13 (8) |
| FST / norms / postings | .10 / disk / disk | .10 / .05 / disk | .10 / .05 / .35 | .10 / .05 / .35 |
| Vector codes | streamed from disk | .55 (newest 35–45 %) | 1.18 (192 bits) | 1.58 |
| Meta + author column | disk | disk | disk | .48 |
| Titles + query cache | .01 | .03 | .05 | .20 |
| **Warm cache** | ≈ .03 | ≈ .24 | ≈ .55 | ≈ 4.9 |

Latency and capacity per level:

| | 1 GB | 2 GB | 4 GB | 10 GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Query embedding | 18 ms | 18 ms | 7.5 ms | 7.5–18 ms |
| Vector search (first stage) | 0.3–0.8 s | 0.15–0.4 s | 0.05–0.3 s | 0.05–0.3 s |
| **Cold query** (no cache hits, top-100) | ≈ 4–5 s | ≈ 3.7–4.5 s | ≈ 3.0–3.4 s | ≈ 3.0–3.4 s |
| **Warm query** (all candidates cached) | ≈ 0.4–0.9 s | ≈ 0.2–0.5 s | ≈ 0.1–0.35 s | ≈ 0.1–0.35 s |
| Repeated query | < 10 ms | < 10 ms | < 10 ms | < 10 ms |
| Warm capacity: fully warmed / prefix-only documents | 30k / 180k | 0.25M / 1.4M | 0.55M / 3.2M | ~5M / ~28M |
| Time to fill (idle CPU) | < 1.5 h | 2–12 h | 5–27 h | 2–10 days, or instant with a persistent sidecar |

Latencies are estimates except the embedding times.
- **Cold query cost:** 2.8 s of decoding (6.5k tokens at 2,300 tokens/s) + the first-stage vector search + 0.5–1 s of CPU re-embedding contention on the CPU plans + about 0.1 s to fetch results.
- **Partly warm query:** the warm time plus 0.43 ms for each token that has to be decoded.
- **Top-200 rerank:** doubles the decoding part when cold.

## 8. Admission control
- All large working memory is pre-reserved in pools: the KV pool, step scratch, embedder activations and the scan-train ring.
- **`admit()` takes two things:**
  - A concurrency permit: `max_inflight` is 2 / 3 / 4 / 8 by level.
  - A scratch reservation estimated from the query's parameters: `1 MB + 8 B × C × threads + 2 KB × rerank_k + 8 KB × k` (C = first-stage candidate count). That is typically 4–8 MB, capped at 16 MB for k ≤ 100 and 32 MB for k ≤ 500.
- Waiting queries queue in FIFO order with a deadline; when it passes, the call raises `Busy` (HTTP 503).
- **Decoding has a per-query token budget**, about 8k tokens (≈ 3.5 s).
  - Candidates are decoded in first-stage order; cache hits are free. Warm caches therefore give deeper reranks (100 grows to 200).
  - At the budget or deadline, the remaining candidates keep their first-stage score ("anytime" rerank).
  - Under backlog the budget shrinks; top-50 costs −0.013 P@10 (E27).
- `k` is limited to the plan (500 maximum; 100 over HTTP).

## 9. Background pre-warming
- **Priority list:** after the loader finishes, one pass over the metadata blocks (about 0.2 s on 16 threads, E) builds it.
  - Utility = recency + log1p(root story's descendants or score), with a boost at runtime for keys found in the ghost queue.
  - Size: 1.5 × the cache capacity, at 8 B per entry.
- **Order of work:**
  1. Titles of the top ~1 million stories (about 1.8 h, about 75 MB).
  2. Prefixes of the newest months.
  3. Top threads, prefixes and embeddings.
  4. Recently evicted candidates.
- **When it runs:**
  - only after ≥ 100 ms with no interactive work, and on AC power by default;
  - using at most half the slots;
  - parked instantly when a query arrives.
- **Rate:** about 120k documents/h with the iGPU, about 90k/h on CPU-only plans (E).

## 10. L2 disk cache: the decision
- **Default off.** At rest, the only bytes on disk are the archive.
- **`disk_cache="temp"`.** A file in %TEMP% opened with `FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE`, so it disappears even after a crash.
  - Default cap: min(2 × budget, 4 GB).
  - Worth it at 1–2 GB budgets after a few hours of uptime: a hit costs about 0.1 ms, against about 30 ms to decode.
- **`disk_cache=<path>`.** A persistent sidecar (about 1 KB per warmed document), validated against build_id and the embed-configuration id. Days of warm-up then reload in under a second.
- **Rewrite of `cache.rs`:**
  - no `read_to_end` at open;
  - positional reads instead of seek and read under a global mutex;
  - a ring of 64 MB segment files instead of clearing everything;
  - the in-RAM index counted in the budget.

## 11. Code that must change before any memory guarantee holds
These paths are unbounded today:
1. **`VecIndex::search`.** One heap per 64K-document chunk plus a concatenation step. On all HN that is about 24 MB at k=10, 240 MB at k=100, and 0.8 GB at k=500 or with type filters. Fix: one bounded heap per thread, or a threshold selection on a histogram of Hamming distances.
2. **`decode_records_each`.** One lockstep batch of every pending record with no slot limit. A full-text query at k=100 needs 0.25–0.4 GB of KV and 39 MB of logits per step; at k=500, 1–2 GB.
3. **The `engine.rs` caches.** Capped by entry count and cleared completely when full.
4. **`L2::open`.** Reads up to 512 MB into RAM at open.
5. **Author names.** Kept as a `Vec<String>` per segment: 110–390 MB across all HN. Fix: one packed global table.
6. **`LmCodec::load`.** Loads the LM tokenizer (10 MB) even though decoding never uses it.
7. **mmap everywhere.** Every touched page grows the working set without being counted.
8. **`serve`.** One `InferRequest` behind a Mutex for all queries.
9. **`pool.rs`.** One global job slot shared by all callers. Fix: the decode service becomes its only caller.

## 12. Open sequence
1. Read the manifests.
2. Measure the host's baseline working set.
3. Load the tokenizer (its 357 MB peak happens while nothing else is loaded).
4. Compile OpenVINO and run one inference (1.9 s on CPU, 3.0–3.4 s on GPU).
5. Reserve the measured amounts.
6. Load the LM.
7. Load the small structures.
8. Run `plan()`.
9. **Ready after about 3–5 s**, serving with streamed indexes.
10. The loader makes indexes resident (about 0.5–1 s for 1.6 GB).
11. The pre-warmer starts.

`set_ram_budget()` shrinks in this order: cache, then the oldest resident vector segments, then postings, then meta, then the KV pool once idle. It grows in the background. It cannot change the device or go below the floor.

parts.risks:
1. **OpenVINO memory is opaque and depends on the version.**
   - Measured: commit is +0.5 GB larger than the working set, and the GPU plugin keeps memory after a model is dropped.
   - Mitigation: measure at every open, pin the OpenVINO version, and choose the device once per process.
   - Commit-based limits such as Job objects or containers will see about 0.5 GB more than the budget.
2. **The FST needs one contiguous buffer.** It sits in the memory floor (0.03–0.3 GB depending on segment granularity) unless the term dictionary becomes blocked.
3. **Unbounded memory paths today:**
   - `VecIndex::search` per-chunk heaps: up to about 0.8 GB per query;
   - lockstep `decode_records_each`: up to 1–2 GB at k=500 with full text;
   - caches capped by entry count with clear-all eviction;
   - L2 loads its whole file at open.

   No memory guarantee holds until these are rewritten.
4. **Paged KV changes the attention loop.** Output must be proved bit-identical with full verification of the three sample segments; otherwise every archive becomes unreadable.
5. **Freed memory may not leave the working set** because of the allocator or fragmentation, which can cause an eviction spiral. Mitigations:
   - the chunk arena with `VirtualFree`;
   - mimalloc purge;
   - working-set feedback with hysteresis;
   - with `scope="hnz"`, feedback only reports and never evicts.
6. **Caches fill slowly.** The rate is limited by CPU decoding (about 120k documents per hour), so large budgets take days to pay off. A restart loses that work unless the persistent sidecar (disk) is enabled.
7. **Background warming competes with queries.** It costs CPU and battery and can slow interactive queries. Parking, idle detection and an AC-power check reduce this but do not remove it.
8. **CPU-only plans have core contention.** The LM's 8 threads, OpenVINO threads and rayon threads compete; core-type and thread-count hints are needed.
9. **The Windows standby cache can hide cold latency** in benchmarks. Cold numbers should be measured with `io="direct"`.
10. **Re-embedding prefixes may not match the simulation.** Re-embedded 128-token prefixes may not equal the full-text embeddings used in the E27 simulation, which would reduce the value of the embedding cache. This is a quality issue, not a memory one.
11. **Tokenizer JSON parse peak (357 MB).** If loading is reordered, the open sequence can briefly exceed small budgets.
12. **The iGPU path depends on the hardware and driver.** Windows Server VMs usually have no GPU, which forces CPU plans. The GPU driver's kernel cache may also write to disk outside the archive.
parts.open_questions:
1. **Scope of the budget.**
   - `scope="hnz"` (default): only memory loaded by hnz.
   - `scope="process"`: the whole Python/FastAPI process, where hnz shrinks its own caches if the host grows.
2. **Temporary disk while running.** Is it acceptable to use temporary disk space (an ephemeral cache deleted on close)? Is a persistent warm sidecar acceptable as an opt-in?
3. **Deployment hardware.** Will the target always have the Intel iGPU, or can it be a server or VM without a GPU? This decides whether the iGPU embedder (about 1.1 GB, 7.5 ms per query, about 200 docs/s) or the CPU one is the default above 4 GB.
4. **Expected query mix.**
   - How often queries filter by date or focus on recent items.
   - How often queries repeat.
   - How many run concurrently.

   This sets pre-warm priorities and `max_inflight`.
5. **Cold-query time limit.** Is "anytime" reranking at a deadline acceptable, or must every query complete the full top-100/200 rerank?
6. **Segment granularity (monthly, yearly or global).** It drives the FST and author-table memory floor.
7. **f16 KV under `MATH_VERSION 3`.** Should it be adopted before the full rebuild of all HN? It halves LM working memory, but its effect on compression is unmeasured.
8. **Rerank embedding dimensions.** Should the cache store 768-d int8 embeddings (772 B) or 512-d (516 B)? 512-d gives 1.5× more cached documents at a small, unmeasured quality cost.
9. **Missing builds.** A dynamic-shape int8 IR (CPU and GPU) and a compact tokenizer must be built and measured. Today's int8 IR cannot be reshaped.

## 0. Key conclusions
- **What you ship:** one read-only file, `hn-<snapshot>.hnzb`, plus the `hnz` engine (Rust → PyO3 wheel, so `import hnz` works; a C ABI and HTTP are optional).
  - About **5.4 GB at 256 bits**, or **5.0 GB at 192 bits**.
  - The file holds everything a query needs: text, metadata, indexes, both models and tokenizers. Each part is pinned by a SHA-256.
- **Query flow:**
  1. A cheap first stage: sign-bit codes + rare-term postings, with flag and date filters applied inline.
  2. The K best candidates are re-ranked by decoding the first ≤128 body tokens of each with the HN LM.
  3. Those decoded prefixes are re-embedded on the iGPU, and exact BM25 for every query term is computed on them.
  4. The scores are fused and the top-k returned.
- **The LM decoder is the capacity limit:** about 2,300 tok/s on 8 threads with 64 slots (E26 verify: 28.7 rec/s × 79.4 tok). That gives about 0.3 balanced queries/s cold for the whole process.
- **Using a big RAM budget:**
  - The budget **cannot unzip LM text at load**: at about 30 records/s, decoding all of HN would take about 19 days.
  - What RAM can do: pin indexes, unpack metadata columns, and cache decoded prefixes and exact embeddings. Each cached candidate saves about 26 ms of LM time.
- **Biggest unmeasured risk:** E27a ("256 bits + top-200 rerank = no significant loss") was measured on 611,640 docs. At 49.3M docs (80× more), the number of candidates K needed for the same recall may be several times larger. This must be measured (E30d) before fixing the bit width and K.

Grounding (files read):
- `C:\Desarrollo\Odoo\AI\HNTurboVec\hnz\src\engine.rs`, `segment.rs`, `meta.rs`, `bm25.rs`, `vecs.rs`, `embed.rs`, `cache.rs`, `textstore.rs`
- `C:\Desarrollo\Odoo\AI\HNTurboVec\hnz\src\lm\store.rs`, `model.rs`, `kernels.rs`, `pool.rs`, `coder.rs`
- `C:\Desarrollo\Odoo\AI\HNTurboVec\pipeline.py`, `embed_month.py`, `bench_rescore.py`
- `C:\Desarrollo\Odoo\AI\HNTurboVec\doc\05-arquitectura.md`, `BITACORA.md` (E10–E29)
- `results_e27.txt`, `results_e28.txt`, `results_final.txt`, `results_build_v4.txt`

## 1. Block layout: one container file
**Why one file:**
- Distribution and replacement are atomic, there is one checksum tree, and a half-copied snapshot is impossible.
- A read-only snapshot does not need per-segment folders.
- Folders stay only for build intermediates (`work/seg-YYYY`) and as a dev "unpacked" mode (`toc.json` plus part files, read by the same reader).
- NTFS/exFAT only; FAT32 is not supported (4 GB file limit).

```
0        Superblock 4 KiB: magic "HNZB\r\n\x1a\n", major=1, minor, features u64, file_len,
         toc_off, toc_len, toc_sha256[32], snapshot_id[16], created, writer[64], crc32c
4 KiB..  parts, each at a 4 KiB-aligned offset (page size; sector size for FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING);
         arrays inside are 64-B aligned; zero padding (~2 KiB/part, <1 MB total)
toc_off  TOC = zstd(JSON {manifest, parts[]})
EOF-64   trailer "HNZBEND\0" + toc_off + toc_sha256 (detects truncation)
```
The whole file is mapped once (memmap2, 64-bit address space), so there is no 64 KiB view-alignment constraint.

**Part entry fields:** `{name, off, len, codec: raw|zstd, raw_len, sha256, access: load|pin|scan|random, meta}`. The `access` class tells the RAM governor how each part is used.

**Parts.** All parts share one global document number ("docnum") = rank of the HN id. Because HN ids grow with time, a date range is a contiguous docnum range.

| Part | Content | Codec / access | All HN |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model/embed.xml`, `model/embed.bin` | EmbeddingGemma-2 text IR, NNCF INT8_ASYM, bounded-dynamic shape [1..32]×[1..256]. One IR serves queries and docs (replaces 5 IRs) | zstd/load; raw/load | 0.4 MB est.; 272.5 MB |
| `model/embed.tok` | `gemma2_tokenizer.json` | zstd/load | 32.2 MB → ~6 MB est. |
| `model/lm.hnzlm` | `lm-hn-70m` (E29) | raw/load | 71.7 MB |
| `meta/blocks`, `meta/index` | meta.rs blocks of 1024 docs using **global** author ids; index = u32 first_id, u32 first_time, u64 off | zstd/random; raw/load | ~0.26 GB; 0.8 MB |
| `meta/flags` | 1 B/doc: `type`, `dead<<3`, `deleted<<4` | zstd/load (49 MB in RAM) | ~6 MB |
| `meta/authors`, `meta/authors.fst` | global author names (frequency order) + name→id FST | zstd/load | ~10–20 MB est. |
| `text/groups`, `text/gidx` | LM records in "lm2" framing (§1.1); u64 offset per 32 docs | raw/random; raw/load | ~2.79 GB; 12 MB |
| `vec/codes`, `vec/has`, `vec/rank` | MRL sign bits, only for docs that have a vector; has-bitmap; u32 rank per 512 docs | raw/scan; load | 1.51 GB @256 bits, 1.14 GB @192; 6.6 MB |
| `lex/terms.fst` | global dictionary of **all** terms → packed u64 | raw/random | 0.05–0.15 GB est. |
| `lex/post` | postings of rare terms only (global df ≤ max_df), BitPacker4x, no tf | raw/random | 0.26–0.39 GB est. |
| `lex/norms` | 1 B/doc length norm (bm25.rs `norm_encode`) | raw/random | 49 MB |
| `verify/report` | build verification report | zstd | <1 MB |

**Manifest contents:**
- n_docs, id and time ranges.
- `lm{sha256, model_id, math_version=2, group=32, framing="lm2", rec_check=true}`
- `embed{sha256, doc_prompt="title: {t|none} | text: {x}", query_prompt="task: search result | query: ", prefix_body_tokens=P, dims=768, code_bits, build_device}`
- `lex{tokenizer_version, k1=1.2, b=0.75, avgdl, N, max_df_abs, with_tf=false}`
- `fusion{w, c}` and the rerank defaults.
- Provenance: dataset revision, SHA-256 of each Parquet, hnz commit.
- Verification summary.

**Integrity:**
- Always checked at open (milliseconds): superblock CRC32C and the TOC SHA-256.
- Per-part SHA-256 (`sha2` crate with SHA-NI), by level:
  - `quick`: hashes the load-class parts (~0.4 GB) while they are loaded.
  - `full`: hashes all parts.
  - `deep`: `full` plus a stratified LM decode sample checked against the per-record check bytes.
- Pinned parts are hashed as they are read.
- Open is refused on: major version mismatch, `MATH_VERSION` ≠ the binary's, or LM/embedder SHA ≠ manifest.

### 1.1 Text: all-LM with "lm2" framing
- **Encoding is unchanged:** each record is arithmetic-coded on its own with the HN LM, in representation "e" (E15), with 1 check byte. The rare non-representable records (0.01%, E18) keep the zstd fallback.
- **Framing changes only the header bytes; payloads are copied byte-for-byte.** Per group of 32 records:
  - `u8 bits_len`, `u8 bits_ntok`, `u8 flags_mode`
  - either one shared flags byte `F` or 16 B of per-record nibbles (mode 2b, lmmap 1b, codec 1b)
  - bit-packed `len[32]` and `ntok[32]`
  - the payloads
- Deleted/empty records get `len = 0` and no byte at all.
- This replaces the varint header (~2 B), the varint length (~1.15 B) and the 1 B empty record. Saving: about 0.9 B/record, plus about 9 MB on the index → **about −0.05 GB (estimate)**.
- `LmStore2::rec(doc) -> RecRef{ntok, flags, zstd, check, payload}` replaces `raw()` + `parse_head()`. Because `ntok` is known before decoding, the KV cache can be reserved exactly.
- **Optional hot tier:** `--hot-months N` stores the newest months with the zstd textstore (+~60 B/doc; 12 months ≈ +0.27 GB) so recent candidates decode in microseconds. Default: 0.

### 1.2 Vectors
- **Codes:** sign bits of the first B MRL dimensions. Default B = 256; B = 192 is an option.
- **Prefix definition:** the codes are computed from the embedding of the **prefix** (§2), so query-time re-embedding reproduces the stored embedding exactly.
- **Only docs with content get a code:** 95.4–97.1% of docs (measured on the 3 sample months), so the code array is 3–5% smaller than a dense one.
- **Scan:** the existing two-stage scan in `vecs.rs` (Hamming, then asymmetric lookup table), with three changes:
  - Flag and time filters are applied **inline** during the scan, which removes the over-sampling and ×4/×16 retry loops.
  - Each thread scans a large chunk (n_range/threads) or uses a u8-distance histogram to select the cutoff. Today's 65k-doc chunks with a C1-sized heap each would merge millions of entries at 49M docs.
  - C1 = max(50·K_v, 20k).

### 1.3 Lexical index
- **One global FST** stores every term with df > 0. Its u64 value is one of:
  - `DF_ONLY{df:26}` — frequent term, no postings
  - `SINGLE{docnum:26}` — term in exactly one doc (49.3M < 2^26)
  - `LIST{df:14, off:40}` — rare term with a postings list
- **Rare** = global df ≤ `max_df_abs`. Default: 0.02% of N ≈ 9,860 docs. E27b used a per-segment 0.02% threshold.
  - A global threshold keeps the index consistent across years. It avoids the E25 problem (a term frequent in one period vanishing only in that period).
- **No tf stored** (−2.1 B/doc, E27b). tf only matters for the first-stage ranking; the final BM25 is recomputed from the decoded text.
- **Frequent terms** keep only their df, which gives an exact IDF. They are scored on the fly over the decoded candidates.
- Postings reuse `encode_postings` and `Cursor` with tf disabled, over global u32 docnums.

### 1.4 Metadata
Unchanged meta.rs blocks (5.5–5.9 B/doc, E26) and the flags column. Authors move to a global dictionary instead of one per segment (≈ −20 MB, estimate).

## 2. Build pipeline (snapshot, no retier)
Steps 1–3 run per year, resumable in `work/seg-YYYY` with `sources.json` as today.

1. **`hnz prompts --prefix-body-tokens 128`** (CPU, minutes):
   - Tokenizes the LM string exactly as `encode_record` does and cuts it at P body tokens.
   - Applies the same prefix-to-text conversion as the query-time decoder.
   - Feeds `prompt::doc_prompt()`, the **same Rust function** used at query time.
   - This replaces Python's `clean()` in `embed_month.py`, so build and query text are identical by construction.
2. **`embed_prompts.py`** on the iGPU (fp16 bucket IRs 32/64/128; the 256 bucket is no longer needed), then `hnz index --bits 256`.
   - About 259 docs/s, derived from E13's per-bucket rates.
   - About 2.1 days with an idle CPU, about 3.3 days while compression runs (E18: ~130 docs/s with the CPU busy).
3. **`hnz build --profile compact --lm models/lm-hn-70m.hnzlm`**: writes meta, lm2 text, and a per-year lexicon in today's format (all terms with tf) as an intermediate.
   - About 115 records/s on 16 threads → **about 5 days for all of HN**.
4. **`hnz pack --out hn-<snap>.hnzb work/seg-*`** (about 1–3 h, estimate):
   - Assigns global docnums, builds the global author dictionary and re-blocks the metadata.
   - Re-groups the lm2 text (payloads copied unchanged).
   - Concatenates the codes and builds has/rank.
   - Does a k-way union of the per-year FSTs (`fst::map::OpBuilder::union`), sums df globally, then either merges a rare term's postings (with docnum offsets) or keeps its df only.
   - Adds the models, zstd-compresses the tokenizer, computes a SHA-256 per part, writes the TOC and superblock.
   - Writes to `.tmp`, fsyncs, then renames.
5. **`hnz verify-block --parquet data/ --lm-sample 0.005`:**
   - Checks all metadata against the Parquet files.
   - Fully checks every zstd-fallback record.
   - Decodes a stratified 0.5% LM sample (about 246k records, about 2.4 h at 28.7 rec/s) and checks each record's check byte.
   - A full LM decode check of all 49.3M records would take **about 20 days of CPU**. It is optional, resumable, and can run in the background.

**pipeline.py changes:**
- New flags: `--profile compact --bits 256 --prefix-body-tokens 128 --max-df 0.0002 --block out/hn-<snap>.hnzb`.
- Steps: `download, prompts, embed, build, index, pack, verify`.
- Removed: the hot/cold split, `--retier`, and the 768/512-bit logic.
- Wall time is about 5 days: compression on the CPU and embedding on the iGPU overlap.

## 3. Query pipeline (compact profile)
**Q0 — Parse.**
- Split the query into BM25 terms (`tokenize.rs`, the same tokenizer used at index time).
- Look up each term in the global FST and classify it:
  - rare → has postings
  - frequent → df only
  - absent → can never match any doc
- IDF = ln((N−df+0.5)/(df+0.5)+1), with the global N and the manifest's avgdl.

**Q1 — Query embedding.** int8 IR, 19–24 ms on CPU (E26). Skipped in keyword mode when all query terms are rare.

**Q2 — Range and filters.**
- Date range → docnum range [lo, hi) from `meta/index` first_time, with an exact check in the two edge blocks (`engine.rs` logic).
- Filter predicate = flags (deleted, dead, types) + the edge time check.
- Author filter → exact candidate set from an unpacked author column if the RAM budget allows, otherwise a scan of the metadata blocks.

**Q3 — Vector stage.**
1. Hamming distance over the codes in [lo, hi), with the filter applied inline → top-C1.
2. Asymmetric lookup-table scoring of those C1 → top-K_v.

**Q4 — Lexical stage.** MaxScore over the rare-term postings (no tf, global IDF, norms), with the filter inline → top-K_b.

**Q5 — Candidate set.**
- U = top-K_v ∪ top-K_b.
- Ordered by s1 = v_asym + w·b_rare/(b_rare + c).
- Presets:

| Preset | K_v | K_b | Expected U |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast | 0 (no rerank) | 0 | — |
| balanced | 100 | 20 | ≈ 120 |
| precise | 200 | 30 | ≈ 230 |

**Q6 — Cache probe.**
- `EmbCache`: doc → int8[768] + scale.
- `PrefixCache`: doc → title, url, plain body prefix, complete flag.
- A hit skips Q7 and Q8 for that candidate.

**Q7 — LM prefix decode.**
- Runs in the shared `DecodeService` (§4).
- Limit: P = 128 **body** tokens; title and url are always decoded in full (same semantics as `limits` today).
- Priority: (query deadline, s1 rank).
- Expected cost: about 60–65 LM tokens per candidate (lognormal fit to E10/E13).
- Records that fit inside the prefix (about 80–85%) are decoded completely, so their check byte is verified for free.

**Q8 — Re-embedding.**
- Runs in `DocEmbedService` on the iGPU, using the same int8 IR with f16 compute.
- Prompt built from the decoded prefix → Gemma tokens → length buckets ≤32 / ≤64 / ≤128 with batch sizes 32 / 32 / 16.
- A bucket is sent when full or 15 ms after its first item.
- Pipelined with Q7: candidates are sent as their decodes finish.
- CPU fallback uses the same IR.

**Q9 — Exact BM25 for all query terms.**
- Text scored: `index_text(title, url host, plain prefix)` — the same text the index is built from.
- tf from the decoded text, document length from `lex/norms`, global IDF (frequent terms included).
- Exact for complete records. For the long ~15% it is a lower bound from the prefix; keyword mode uses P = 256 to reduce this.

**Q10 — Fusion.**
- s = cos_exact + w·b/(b+c).
- w and c must be re-tuned: the asymmetric score is about 0.8 × the cosine, so keeping today's balance gives roughly w ≈ 0.19 (E30c).
- The "must have some signal" rule stays as today.

**Q11 — Fetch the top-k.**
- Metadata rows.
- Snippet = first 64 body tokens of the decoded prefix (no extra cost).
- Story titles: from `TitleCache`, or title-only jobs at high priority (about 15 tokens each). Roots of the current top-20 are submitted speculatively during the rerank.
- Full text: re-decode the records that were not complete (E26: 527 ms median, 1.09 s p90 for 10 results).

**Anytime behaviour.** At the deadline (default 6 s for balanced, 10 s for precise), the query's pending jobs are cancelled.
- The top-k is chosen among the reranked candidates.
- If fewer than k were reranked, the list is filled in s1 order and those items are marked `reranked=false`.
- When the expected total tokens / throughput is below 0.8 × the deadline, the decoder admits the longest records first (it knows `ntok`), which shortens the slow low-occupancy tail. Otherwise it admits by rank.

**Fast path and progressive results.**
- `quality="fast"` returns the Q5 order with 64-token snippets. The top-10 are the first decode jobs anyway, so this work is not wasted.
- `search_iter` yields a preview first, then the final list.

**Other modes:**
- **Keyword mode:** candidates = rare-term postings (exhaustive) ∪ vector top-K_v whenever a query term is frequent. Retrieval for frequent terms is therefore **not exhaustive** — a change in meaning versus today. A result must have exact BM25 > 0.
- **Vector mode:** Q3 plus rerank by cosine only.
- **Listing (no query text):** unchanged.

## 4. Concurrency (one process, many threads)
- **DecodeService** — one scheduler thread owns a `Batch` with S slots (64 by default, 128 if the budget allows) and uses the existing spin pool (8 threads).
  - It runs continuous batching (a generalised `decode_stream`) with an earliest-deadline-first queue.
  - A job is admitted when a slot is free and its KV reservation (24 KB × positions) fits.
  - It cancels jobs when the query is dropped or its deadline passes.
  - An in-flight map (doc → subscribers) deduplicates the same candidate across queries.
  - It replaces today's per-query lock-step `decode_records_each`, where concurrent queries fight over the pool's single job slot.
- **Capacity:** about 2,300 tok/s.
  - Balanced (about 7.3k tokens per query) → about 0.31 queries/s.
  - Precise (about 14k tokens) → about 0.16 queries/s.
  - Engine-side admission: `max_inflight_precise` (default 2) plus a queue. Under overload K is reduced rather than missing deadlines.
- **DocEmbedService:** one thread, the GPU-compiled model, 2 infer requests, micro-batching across queries. Query embeddings jump ahead of doc batches.
- **QueryEmbedder:** a pool of N infer requests on one compiled model, replacing `Mutex<Embedder>`.
- **First-stage scans:** a separate rayon pool of 8 threads.
- **Python:** the engine is `Send + Sync` behind an `Arc`, and every call releases the GIL.

## 5. RAM this subsystem needs (to be granted by the budget manager)
All figures are estimates to be measured.

**Fixed:**
- Embedder on the GPU: 0.35–0.45 GB. Add 0.3–0.4 GB if a separate CPU copy is kept for queries.
- Gemma tokenizer: 0.06–0.12 GB.
- LM: 0.075 GB.
- Flags: 0.049 GB.
- Small indexes (authors, text index, meta index, has/rank): about 0.04 GB.
- **Total: about 0.6–1.1 GB.**

**Working memory:**
- LM KV cache: 24 KB per position per slot. At S = 64 that is about 0.1 GB on average and 0.26 GB worst case.
- A 2,000-token full record needs 48 MB per slot.
- Logits: 13 MB. Re-embedding activations: about 0.1 GB.

**Elastic, in priority order:**
1. Pin the codes (1.14 / 1.51 GB).
2. `TitleCache` + metadata block cache (≤0.2 GB).
3. `EmbCache` (0.8 KB per doc) + `PrefixCache` (0.3 KB per doc).
4. Unpacked author and parent columns (0.15 / 0.2 GB).
5. Pin the lexical parts (0.36–0.59 GB).
6. Raise to S = 128 slots (+0.23 GB).
7. Pin the text (2.79 GB).

**Example budgets:**
- **2 GB:** codes are streamed (0.25–0.45 s per query when they are not in the OS cache); 0.3–0.5 GB of caches.
- **4 GB:** codes and lexical parts pinned; about 1 GB of caches.
- **10 GB:** everything pinned; about 4 GB of caches (about 3M cached candidates).

**Idle warming (optional):** decode and embed by prior (score, recency) at about 38 docs/s (about 136k per hour).

## 8. Measurements needed before implementing

parts.risks:
1. **Corpus-size effect on K (the biggest risk).**
   - E27a's "no loss at 256 bits + top-200" was measured on 611k docs; the real archive is 80× larger.
   - A simple bivariate-normal model (correlation 0.9 between binary and exact scores) puts top-10 recall at top-200 at about 91% on 611k docs. At 49.3M it drops to about 59%, and getting back to about 91% needs K ≈ 1,800.
   - If real data behaves like that, precise queries cost tens of seconds — or more bits are needed (384 bits = +0.75 GB).
   - Many filtered or date-ranged queries scan far fewer docs, so they are less exposed.
   - Must be measured (E30d) before choosing bits and K.
2. **Prefix-embedding definition not validated.** E27a re-ranked with stored full embeddings (≤256 Gemma tokens, Python `clean()`). The plan uses a P = 128 body-token prefix and Rust prompts at both build and query time. If quality drops, use P ≈ 256–300 (+17% decode cost). Must be measured (E30a).
3. **The LM decoder is the single capacity limit** (about 2,300 tok/s): about 0.3 balanced or 0.16 precise cold queries per second for the whole process. FastAPI concurrency cannot raise this; concurrent queries share it and wait. Needs deadlines, admission control and K reduction under load. Throughput gains (bigger S, faster kernels, the cascade rerank) are not measured.
4. **CPU contention on the hybrid 6P+8E+2LPE CPU:** the spin pool (8 threads), scans, OpenVINO host threads and Python all compete. E20 already found the spin pool hogging the CPU when other heavy work runs. p90 under 2–4 concurrent clients is unknown; may need thread QoS or affinity tuning.
5. **RAM accounting:**
   - OpenVINO's CPU and GPU plugins allocate memory we cannot see directly, and the iGPU uses shared system RAM.
   - Pages of memory-mapped parts and the OS standby cache blur the meaning of "process RAM".
   - Every fixed-footprint figure here is an estimate and must be measured at the 2, 4 and 10 GB budgets.
6. **Lossless guarantee in practice:** a full decode check of 49.3M LM records costs about 20 days of CPU.
   - The default is a 0.5% sample, plus decode equivalence by construction (prefill and step run identical per-position operations), plus 637k records already fully verified (E24/E26), plus per-record check bytes at read time.
   - A silent mismatch in records nobody has sampled stays possible, though unlikely.
   - Prefix decodes are only covered by the model SHA and `MATH_VERSION` checks.
7. **Keyword mode changes meaning:** frequent terms (df > 0.02%) are no longer retrieved exhaustively. Keyword-only quality will probably be below today's 0.227 (it was 0.141 without on-the-fly BM25).
8. **On-the-fly BM25 is approximate for the ~15% of long records** (tf comes from the prefix only), and the fusion weights (w, c) were tuned for asymmetric scores (asym ≈ 0.8 × cos), so they need re-tuning.
9. **Global rare-term index size** is not measured: bursty terms under a global threshold, plus the size of a global FST over all vocabulary. Estimate 0.36–0.59 GB.
10. **OpenVINO API and performance unknowns:**
    - openvino-rs 0.11 may not expose loading a model from memory with a host-pointer weights tensor. Fallback: copy the weights (+272 MB at load) or extract to `%TEMP%`.
    - Bounded-dynamic shapes plus int8 weights on the Arc GPU plugin are not benchmarked.
    - A GPU compile cache would add about 0.3 GB on disk.
11. **Build length and rework:** about 5 days of CPU (iGPU in parallel); any format or math bug found later means a full rebuild. The HN LM and the embedder must be pinned by SHA in the manifest.
12. **Fast-path quality is much lower** (0.183 vs 0.229 vector-only). Clients must check `reranked` / `degraded` and not treat preview results as final.
13. **Long full-text decodes are slow:** a 2,000-token record takes seconds at low batch occupancy (E26 p90 for full text is 1.09 s), which can hurt RAG use of the top-k.
