plan.architecture:
## 1. The deliverable: one self-contained block
- **Code.** A Rust core crate `hnz` (lib) with thin front-ends, Windows x86-64-v3 only:
  - `hnz-py`: PyO3 abi3 wheel `hnz-<v>-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl`, so `import hnz` works on Python ≥3.10.
  - `hnz-cli`: `hnz.exe` with prompts/build/pack/verify-block/inspect/search/serve. HTTP covers other languages.
  - `hnz-capi` (optional, Phase 6): `hnz.dll` + `hnz.h`, JSON in and out.
- **Data.** One read-only directory `hn-YYYY-MM.hnz\` holding:
  - `hn.hnzb`: a container with all data, the LM, both tokenizers and the manifest, with an xxh3 hash per part.
  - `embed.xml` / `embed.bin`: the EmbeddingGemma-2 int8 OpenVINO IR.
  - Size ≈5.45 GB at 256 bits, ≈5.1 GB at 192 bits [E, summed from measured components].
  - Nothing else is on disk at rest by default: no L2 file and no compile cache.
- **Runtime dependency.** The OpenVINO DLLs from the `openvino` pip package. hnz finds them on disk and never imports the package.
- **Process model.** One `Archive` per process, thread-safe, with the GIL released.
  - `ram=` caps everything hnz holds: models, OpenVINO CPU/iGPU memory, indexes, LM working memory, caches and per-query scratch.

## 2. How the three designs were merged
D1 = API/packaging design, D2 = RAM/caches design, D3 = block/pipeline design.

| # | Topic | Proposals | Decision and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Block shape | D1: directory of ≤7 files. D3: one `.hnzb` including the embedder | **Container + 2 IR files.** You said several files are fine ("varios archivos"). OpenVINO reads the IR natively: no 272 MB weight copy and no unsafe host-pointer path. Atomic per-part checksums are kept. A single file stays a later option. |
| 2 | Corpus layout | D1: per-segment parts packed together. D3: global docnums | **Global docnum** (rank of the HN id; deleted rows kept as metadata) forming **one logical `Seg`**. This gives one FST, global df and threshold (which on-the-fly BM25 needs), one author table, and no cross-segment merge or retry code. The build stays per year (LM text) and per month (embeddings); `pack` assembles everything. |
| 3 | I/O and residency | D1: mmap everything. D2: private resident copies + positional reads. D3: map the whole file | **D2.** `Blob::{Resident, Disk}`, with no data mmap by default. Touched mapped pages land in the process working set (WS), where they can be neither attributed nor capped. Avoiding mmap is what makes "≤ ram" testable. |
| 4 | LM working memory | D1/D3: exact reservation from `ntok`. D2: paged KV + parking | **Exact KV capacity per job** (`KvCache::with_capacity`, no doubling), charged to a fixed KV byte pool. The need is known at admission: `min(ntok, cap(want)) × 24,576 B`, because Prefix means "≤P body tokens and ≤T_cap tokens in total". No paging or parking is needed. KV layout and arithmetic order are unchanged, so output is bit-identical by construction. |
| 5 | Embedder device | D1/D3: CPU for queries + GPU for docs. D2: one device chosen by budget | **One int8 dynamic-shape IR on one device per process.** GPU when ram ≥ 4 GB, device=auto and an Intel GPU is present; CPU otherwise. Queries and doc re-embedding share it through an InferRequest pool plus a batcher. The GPU plugin does not return memory (M), and a second copy costs 0.4–0.9 GB. |
| 6 | Text that gets embedded per document | Today: Python `clean()` on raw HTML, ≤256 Gemma tokens. D3: a prefix built by one Rust function | **D3, gated by E30a.** `prompt::doc_prompt()` runs over the first P body LM tokens (P=128, T_cap=224 tentative; stored in the manifest). `hnz prompts` uses it at build time and the reranker at query time, so re-embedding reproduces the stored embedding with no Python/Rust drift. |
| 7 | Keyword index | E27b: per-month 0.02 % threshold. D3: global | **Global df and global threshold** (df ≤ max_df_abs ≈ 9,860 = 0.02 % of N). Rare terms get postings without term frequency (tf). Frequent terms are DF-only FST entries (exact IDF) and are scored on the decoded candidates. |
| 8 | Caches | D1: sharded LRU. D2: S3-FIFO on a VirtualAlloc arena. D3: five caches | **One generic byte-weighted sharded cache `WCache`** (16 shards, S3-FIFO/CLOCK, weight = real heap bytes + 64), used four times: EmbCache, TextCache (token ids), QueryCache, MetaBlockCache. All are `Evictable`. The disk L2 cache is **off**; an opt-in persistent warm file is Phase 7. |
| 9 | Time limits | D1: hard timeout. D2/D3: anytime deadline | **`deadline` is anytime.** At the deadline, pending decode jobs are cancelled and the call returns the reranked part plus a fill in first-stage order, with `degraded=True`. `queue_timeout` raises BusyError, and there is a `cancel` token. TimeoutError is raised only if the first stage itself misses the deadline. |
| 10 | API | D1: `open()`/`Archive`. D2: `set_ram_budget`, `warm`. D3: `quality`, `search_iter` | **D1 surface + `quality` presets + `deadline`.** No runtime `set_ram_budget` in v1; `search_iter` in Phase 6; `warm()` in Phase 7. |
| 11 | LM scheduling | All three: one scheduler thread | **DecodeService**, a generalised `decode_stream`: continuous batching; Interactive > Fetch > Background, earliest deadline first inside each class; cancel and deadline; in-flight dedup (Title ⊂ Prefix ⊂ Full). It is the only user of the spin pool. |
| 12 | Pre-warming | D2: background warming when idle | **Off by default**, because a library should not burn CPU unasked. Opt-in later. |

## 3. Runtime components
```
callers: Python threads (GIL released) · HTTP workers · C ABI
   │  api::Archive = Arc<Inner> (Send+Sync)
   ▼
Admission ── FIFO permits (max_concurrent) + per-query scratch Reservation (queue_timeout → Busy)
   ├─ EmbedService ── OpenVINO int8 IR on CPU|GPU · queries: InferRequest pool · docs: batcher thread (buckets ≤32/64/128/256)
   ├─ Engine stage 1 ── per-archive rayon pool

```
- **Block/Blob.** The container has a superblock and a TOC, and every part is a `Blob`:
  - `Resident`: a private 4 KiB-aligned copy, reserved in the budget.
  - `Disk`: positional reads through a pool of 8 file handles. Windows serialises I/O per synchronous handle, hence the pool.
- **Engine.** Today's logic is kept (listing, exact scans, date edges, fetch/root walk), now over one logical segment.
  - Stage 1 is rewritten with inline filters (flags + a time bitmap for the two edge blocks) and bounded per-thread heaps.
  - This removes the ×4/×16 retry loop.
- **DecodeService.** Owns a `Batch` with ≤S slots.
  - Admits jobs by priority and deadline when both a slot and enough KV bytes are free.
  - A head-of-line reservation keeps 2,000-token Full jobs from starving.
  - Streams `Decoded{docnum, ids, flags, complete}` back to tickets; dropping a ticket cancels its jobs.
- **EmbedService.** Compiles once and warms up at the maximum shape (16×256) to measure its memory.
  - Each in-flight query uses its own InferRequest.
  - Doc batches are sent when full, or 15 ms after their first item.
  - Every embedding is quantised to `EmbI8` before scoring, so cached and fresh paths rank identically.
- **Two profiles, one engine.**
  - The compact block is the deliverable.
  - Today's segment directories (the "fast" profile, 10.4 GB) are kept for development and as an option.
  - `hnz.open` opens both; the rerank stage runs only for compact.

## 4. Life of a query (compact, hybrid)
1. Admission.
2. Parse terms and look up their FST classes.
3. Embed the query.
4. Map since/until to a docnum range and build the filter mask.
5. Stage 1: vector top-K_v ∪ rare-term top-K_b.
6. Probe the caches.
7. Submit Prefix decode jobs in stage-1 order.
8. Re-embed each prefix as soon as it is decoded.
9. Compute exact BM25 on the decoded text.
10. Fuse the scores (anytime cut at the deadline).
11. Fetch: snippets come from the prefixes, story titles from Title jobs, and full text from optional Full jobs.
12. Store the ranked list in the QueryCache.

Per-step budgets are in `query_pipeline`.

## 5. Threads
- **LM:** `threads` spin threads. Default 8 (logical/2); measured best, 8 ≫ 16 (E17).
  - Only DecodeService calls `SpinPool::run`.
  - This removes E17's oversubscription pathology (17.3 s vs 1.03 s per batch) under concurrency.
- **Stage 1:** a per-archive rayon pool of `threads`; the global pool is never used.
- **OpenVINO on CPU plans:** INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS=4, NUM_STREAMS=2, set on the Core before compiling.
- **Other threads:** 1 doc batcher, 1 sampler (1 Hz), 1 loader. Worker threads never call into Python.
- **Capacity.** Cold work is bound by the LM (≈2,300 tok/s, M), so the process handles ≈0.3 cold balanced queries/s. Concurrency serves warm queries and queues cold ones.

## Semantics
- **Dates (`since`, `until`).**
  - A string such as `"2015"`, `"2015-06"` or `"2015-06-01"` is an inclusive period, parsed by `dates::parse` as in the CLI; `until="2018-06"` includes all of June.
  - An int (epoch) or a datetime is an exact instant, applied as since ≤ t < until. Naive datetimes are treated as UTC.
  - A `date` means whole days, inclusive.
- **`types` and `author`.** `types` takes one kind or several. `author` is an exact, case-sensitive match.
- **`quality` presets** (K values tentative until E30d):
  - `fast`: stage 1 only, plus 64-token snippets. Preview quality: vector-only P@10 0.183 vs 0.229 [M, E27a].
  - `balanced`: reranks ≈100 vector + 20 keyword candidates by decoding prefixes of ≤128 body tokens, re-embedding them and computing exact BM25.
  - `precise`: ≈200 + 30 candidates.
- **`k` and `offset`.**
  - `k + offset ≤ 500`.
  - At most max(K_v, min(k + offset, 200)) candidates are reranked; the rest keep stage-1 order with `reranked=False`.
  - The ranked list is kept in the QueryCache, so the next page is instant.
- **`deadline` (anytime).**
  - At the deadline, unstarted decode jobs are cancelled.
  - The answer is the best reranked hits, filled in stage-1 order, with `degraded=True`.
  - TimeoutError is raised only if stage 1 itself cannot finish.
- **`mode`.**
  - `keyword` on a compact block finds rare terms exhaustively.
  - Frequent terms only match within the vector candidates, and a warning says so. Without the semantic runtime, a query made only of frequent terms returns nothing.
- **`text`.**
  - `none`: metadata only.
  - `title`: ≈15–30 LM tokens per cold record.
  - `snippet`: title, url and the first 64 body tokens; free for reranked hits.
  - `full`: lossless HTML plus plain text.
- **`raw=True`.** Returns plain dicts with exactly the JSON schema used by HTTP and the C ABI.
- **RAM.**
  - `ram` caps the RAM attributable to hnz: process WorkingSetSize minus the working set measured at the start of `open()`.
  - Excluded: the OS file cache, Python result objects, and untouched commit.
  - `open()` raises `BudgetError(required, budget)` when the mandatory floor does not fit.

## Errors
Defined in `python/hnz/errors.py`; Rust maps `HnzError` onto them.
- `Error(Exception)` is the base class:
  - `BlockNotFoundError(Error, FileNotFoundError)`
  - `IncompatibleBlockError` with `.what`, `.block`, `.supported`, `.hint` (format, MATH_VERSION, LM or embedder id, OpenVINO minimum)
  - `CorruptBlockError` with `.component`, `.detail` (hash mismatch, record check byte, canary, truncation)
  - `RuntimeMissingError(Error, ImportError)`: OpenVINO missing, too old or conflicting, or no AVX2
  - `BudgetError(Error, MemoryError)` with `.required`, `.budget`
  - `QueryError(Error, ValueError)`
  - `BusyError`
  - `TimeoutError(Error, builtins.TimeoutError)`
  - `CancelledError`
  - `ClosedError(Error, RuntimeError)`
  - `InternalError(Error, RuntimeError)`: a Rust panic was caught; the archive stays usable.

## Thread safety
- Every method may be called concurrently from any thread, and all Rust work runs with the GIL released (`py.detach`).
- `close()` waits for in-flight calls up to `timeout`, then cancels them.
  - After that, every call raises `ClosedError` and every file handle is closed, so the block can be replaced or deleted.
- Hot swap: `new = hnz.open(new_dir)`, switch the reference, then `old.close()`. Both budgets apply while both are open.
- `asearch` / `aget` run on a worker thread and fire a `CancelToken` on `CancelledError`.

## What `ram` means
- **Covered.** `ram` caps the resident memory attributable to hnz: process WorkingSetSize minus the working set measured at the start of `open()`. It includes:
  - models and tokenizers;
  - the OpenVINO compiled model and its activations, on CPU or iGPU. iGPU memory is system RAM and shows up in the process working set (measured).
  - LM weights, KV cache and logits;
  - resident index parts and caches;
  - per-query scratch, reserved at admission;
  - thread stacks.
- **Not covered:**
  - the OS standby file cache filled by buffered reads. The system owns it and can reclaim it; `io="direct"` bypasses it.
  - Python objects of returned results.
  - untouched commit. OpenVINO commits about +0.5 GB at `Core()` that it never touches (measured). A Job-object commit limit, if one is used, must be at least ram + 0.6 GB.
- **Minimum.** The semantic floor is ≈1.0–1.1 GB [E]; ≥2 GB is recommended. At 1 GB the block opens in keyword/listing mode, or in semantic mode after the Phase 7 model slimming.

**What "decompressing part of the block into RAM" can and cannot mean.**

## Open sequence
1. Read the superblock and TOC (<5 ms) and measure the baseline working set.
2. Load the Gemma tokenizer first, so its 357 MB parse peak happens while nothing else is loaded.
3. Compile OpenVINO and warm it up at the maximum shape: ≈2 s on CPU (M: 1.9 s for b1_s64), ≈3–10 s on GPU.
4. Reserve the measured working-set deltas ×1.1.
5. Load the LM, flags, norms, indexes, author table and FST.
6. Run `plan()`, which raises BudgetError with a per-component breakdown if the floor does not fit.
7. Decode the canaries (0.2–0.3 s).
8. Ready after ≈3–5 s on CPU, ≈5–12 s on GPU [E]. The background loader then pins parts according to the plan.

## Enforcement mechanism
1. **Budget with RAII reservations.**
   - `Budget{limit, used[Model, Index, Working, Cache, Opaque]}`.
   - Every resident part, pool and cache holds a `Reservation`, with `grow`/`shrink` and release on drop.
   - `reserve()` evicts from the Cache class and never blocks; `reserve_wait(deadline, cancel)` is used for admission.
2. **Opaque native memory is measured, not guessed.** The tokenizer and OpenVINO are reserved at their measured working-set delta around load plus max-shape warm-up. The device is chosen once per process because the GPU plugin does not return memory.
3. **Planner order:** floor → device → pools → vector codes (newest first) → postings → metadata → caches (whatever remains, minus 3 %).
4. **Fixed pools.**
   - DecodeService admits a job only when `min(ntok, cap(want)) × 24,576 B` fits in the KV byte pool.
   - Logits and sampling buffers are preallocated.
   - Embedder activations are covered by the warm-up measurement.
   - Stream buffers for stage 1 (4 MB per task) come out of the query ticket.
5. **Admission.**
   - FIFO permits plus a per-query reservation of 1 MB + 8 B·C1·threads + 2 KB·K + 16 KB·k (+ stream buffers when codes are not resident).
   - Capped at 16 MB for k ≤ 100 and 32 MB for k ≤ 500.
   - Waiting longer than `queue_timeout` raises BusyError.
6. **No unbounded paths remain:**
   - Hamming search heaps are bounded per thread to C1;
   - there is no lockstep decode of every pending record;
   - caches are weighted in bytes;
   - no L2 file is read whole at open;
   - authors are a packed table;
   - the LM tokenizer is not loaded at query time.
7. **Feedback loop.**
   - A sampler thread reads GetProcessMemoryInfo once per second (WS, PrivateWS, PrivateUsage), plus DXGI QueryVideoMemoryInfo for the iGPU share (reporting only).
   - If WS − baseline exceeds ram − 2 %, caches are evicted down to ram − 5 % and admission pauses until memory is back under the limit (hysteresis).
   - A CreateMemoryResourceNotification low-memory signal shrinks the caches by 25 %.
   - mimalloc is the global allocator, so freed pages go back to the OS.
   - Tests use a counting-allocator feature that checks reservations ≥ live Rust heap.

## Container format (`hn.hnzb`)
```
0         superblock, 4 KiB: magic "HNZB\r\n\x1a\n", format {major=1, minor, min_reader}, features u64, file_len,
          toc_off, toc_len, toc_xxh3_128, snapshot_id[16], created, writer[64], crc32c
4 KiB..   parts, each starting at a 4 KiB-aligned offset (compatible with FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING); arrays inside 64 B-aligned
toc_off   TOC = zstd(JSON {manifest, parts[]}); part entry = {name, off, len, codec raw|zstd, raw_len, xxh3_128, access load|pin|scan|random}
EOF-64    trailer "HNZBEND\0" + toc_off + toc_xxh3 (detects truncation)
```
- **Docnum.** Global docnum = rank of the HN id. Deleted rows are kept as metadata-only docs, so a date range is a contiguous docnum range.

plan.query_pipeline:
## Steps of a compact hybrid query
Setup for this table:
- Preset `balanced`: K_v = 100 vector candidates, K_b = 20 keyword candidates, so U ≈ 115 candidates; k = 10.
- Machine idle; whole-HN block.
- Cold = empty caches, fresh process, vector codes resident (4 GB plan) unless noted.
- Warm = all candidates already in EmbCache and TextCache, query cache disabled.

| # | Step | Cold | Warm | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Admission: permit + scratch reservation | <0.1 ms + queue wait | same | E |
| 1 | Parse terms (BM25 tokenizer); FST lookup classifies each as Rare{df, post}, Frequent{df} or Absent; global IDF | 1–5 ms | <0.1 ms | E |
| 2 | Query embedding: "task: search result \| query: …" | CPU 18–24 ms; GPU ≈7.5 ms | same | M (static IRs) |
| 3 | since/until → docnum range [lo, hi) via meta/index plus a time check in the 2 edge blocks. Filter mask = flags + edge bitmap. Author → id via FST | <1 ms. Author filter: +0.1–0.3 s scanning metadata blocks, or ms with the 10 GB author column | same | E |
| 4 | Vector stage: Hamming distance over codes in [lo, hi) with the filter applied inline, bounded per-thread heaps → C1 = max(50·K_v, 20k) → asymmetric LUT scoring → top K_v | ≈47M codes: resident 30–60 ms, streamed 0.25–0.5 s | 30–60 ms | E |
| 5 | Keyword stage: MaxScore over rare-term postings (tf=1, global IDF, norms, filter inline) → top K_b | 1–10 ms | same | E |
| 6 | Candidate set U = union, ordered by s1 = v_asym + w·b/(b+c) | <1 ms | same | C |
| 7 | Probe EmbCache / TextCache | µs | all hits | C |
| 8 | Decode misses with DecodeService Prefix jobs (Interactive priority, query deadline, s1 order): ≤P = 128 body tokens, ≤T_cap = 224 in total, ≈61 LM tokens per candidate | ≈7k tokens ≈3.0 s at 2,300 tok/s, +0.1–0.4 s tail | 0 | M rate × D token counts |
| 9 | Re-embedding, pipelined with step 8: doc_prompt → Gemma tokens → buckets ≤32/64/128/256 → batches → EmbI8 | GPU: +0.05–0.15 s tail. CPU int8 ≈50 docs/s: +0.5–1 s because of core contention | 0 | D/E |
| 10 | Exact BM25 for every query term on index_text(title, url host, decoded prefix): tf from the text, dl from norms, global IDF | 1–3 ms | same | E |
| 11 | Fusion: s = cos(EmbI8) + w·b/(b+c), with w and c re-tuned (E30c, ≈0.19 expected) | <1 ms | same | C |
| 12 | Fetch the top-k: meta rows (MetaBlockCache), snippets from the decoded prefixes (free), thread-root walk, story titles from TextCache or Title jobs (≈20 tokens each, submitted speculatively during step 8) | 50–120 ms | 2–10 ms | E |
| 12b | Only with text="full": Full jobs at Fetch priority for records not complete in their prefix (≈15 %) | +0.53 s p50 / 1.09 s p90 | 2–24 ms | M (E26) |
| 13 | Return; QueryCache stores the ranked list (≤200 entries) plus the query vector for pagination | <1 ms | — | C |

**Rules that apply to every query:**
- **Anytime.** At the deadline (balanced 6 s, precise 12 s, fast 2 s) pending jobs are cancelled. The top-k is filled with reranked hits first, then in s1 order (`reranked=False`), and the result is marked `degraded=True`.
- **Per-query token budget.** Balanced 8k tokens, precise 16k. Under backlog — when the expected queue wait exceeds deadline/2 — K_v is halved and a warning is added.
- **Determinism.** Scores always use the quantised EmbI8 vector, so cold and warm runs rank identically. Results are also independent of RAM residency: stage 1 is exact whether codes are resident or streamed.

## End-to-end totals (single query, idle machine, whole-HN block; estimates except M rows above)
| Preset | Cold p50 | Warm p50 | Repeated |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast: no rerank, 64-token snippets of the top 10 | 0.35–0.6 s (0.6–0.9 s with streamed codes) | 60–100 ms | <10 ms |
| balanced: ≈115 candidates | GPU ≈3.3–3.8 s; CPU ≈3.8–4.8 s | 80–150 ms | <10 ms |
| precise: ≈230 candidates | GPU ≈6.3–7 s; CPU ≈7–8.5 s | 100–200 ms | <10 ms |

- p90 ≈ p50 + 0.5–1.5 s (long records), bounded by the deadline.
- For comparison, today's fast profile (M, E26): hot hybrid 25.9 ms; cold fragments 280 ms; full cold text of 10 results 527 ms. The compact profile trades ≈3.5 s of cold latency for half the disk.

## Concurrency
- **Cold queries share the LM.** It decodes ≈2,300 tok/s for the whole process, so capacity is ≈0.3 balanced cold queries/s (≈19 per minute) or ≈0.16 precise per second.
- **Two cold queries at once take ≈6–8 s each.** Within a priority class the earliest deadline runs first, so the first query finishes first rather than both slowing down equally.
- **Warm queries are not LM-bound.** Ten or more queries/s; their limits are permits and stage-1 cores.

## Other paths
- **Listing (no query text).** Newest-first scan of metadata blocks; type filters go through flags. 2–6 ms, plus text decodes for k results (≈20 tokens per title, ≈80 per snippet).
- **Keyword mode.** Candidates are rare-term postings (exhaustive), plus the vector top-K_v when any query term is frequent. They are decoded, scored with exact BM25, and must have BM25 > 0. A query term that appears in no document makes the result empty. Without the semantic runtime, queries with only frequent terms return nothing (with a warning).
- **Vector mode.** Steps 2, 4, 7–9 and 11.
- **Rare types (job, poll, pollopt).** Exact scan of the flags column, then scoring with steps 4–11 restricted to the matching docs.
- **`get(id)`.** id → docnum (meta index + 1 block decode) → Full job at Fetch priority. ≈0.2–0.6 s cold (E26 /item p50 326 ms); µs if TextCache holds the complete record.

- Hot tier: recent-range queries <= 0.3 s.
- Author postings: author filter <= 20 ms at any budget.
Every size change is measured on the sample block and projected to 49.3 M.

plan.risks:
1. **Corpus size versus the rerank depth K (biggest risk).**
   - E27a's "256 bits + top-200 ≈ no loss" was measured on 611k docs. All of HN is 80× larger, so the binary first stage may need K ≈ 500–2,000 for the same recall (model estimate).
   - That would mean cold queries of 10–40 s, or 384-bit codes (+0.75 GB on disk).
   - Mitigation:
     - measure E30d before pack;
     - keep sign bits for 384 dims, so the bit width is chosen at pack time;
     - inline filters shrink the scanned set for date-restricted queries;
     - anytime deadline;
     - cascade rerank (Phase 7).
2. **Prefix-embedding fidelity (E30a).** Codes and rerank built from ≤128-token prefixes, and the Rust prompt function, are not validated yet. Fallback: P = 256 (+≈17 % decode cost).
3. **LM decoding is the only capacity limit.**
   - ≈2,300 tok/s means ≈0.3 cold balanced queries/s per process; more concurrency only adds queueing.
   - Mitigation: caches and QueryCache, admission control with BusyError, presets, cascade rerank, faster kernels / more slots (E30g).
4. **CPU contention on the 6P+8E+2LPE CPU.**
   - The 8 LM spin threads, OpenVINO and rayon all compete. With competing pools a batch took 17.3 s instead of 1.03 s (E17).
   - Mitigation: one LM submitter, per-archive pools, OpenVINO thread caps, GPU offload, and p90 measured with 2–4 clients.
5. **Opaque native memory.**
   - OpenVINO CPU and GPU allocations change between versions; the GPU plugin keeps its memory after a model is dropped; commit exceeds the working set by ≈0.5 GB.
   - Mitigation: measure at open with a max-shape warm-up, fix the device per process, pin the OpenVINO version range, run the working-set feedback loop.
6. **Bit-exactness.**
   - Any change to LM arithmetic order or toolchain after the 5-day compression would make the archive unreadable.
   - Mitigation:
     - the exact-capacity KV cache keeps the memory layout;
     - canaries decoded at open;
     - re-verify the 637k sample records on every change;
     - CI for each kernel (scalar/avx2/vnni);
     - keep every MATH_VERSION decoder; never use mul_add or fast-math;
     - freeze the LM and MATH_VERSION before the full run (f16 KV is excluded).
7. **Keyword-only mode changes meaning.**
   - Frequent terms are no longer searched exhaustively.
   - Without the semantic runtime, a query made only of frequent terms returns nothing.
   - Keeping frequent-term postings would cost ≈1.4–1.8 GB [E, from E27b].
8. **Build cost and rework.**
   - ≈5 days of CPU plus 2–3 days of iGPU.
   - A pack or format bug costs a re-pack (≈1–3 h); an LM or prompt bug costs days.
   - The build needs ≈20–30 GB of scratch disk on top of the Parquet files.
9. **Lossless assurance at full scale is sampled.** It rests on a 0.5 % decode sample plus the check byte validated on every full decode. A full check would take ≈20 days of CPU.
10. **Windows specifics.**
    - Synchronous file handles serialise I/O, hence the handle pool.
    - The standby file cache hides cold latency, so benchmarks must use io=direct or flush it.
    - Files cannot be replaced while open, so close() must drop every handle.
    - Another openvino.dll loaded first in the process wins; the loader checks the version and refuses.
    - Wheels built with the GNU toolchain may import MinGW runtime DLLs; gate with objdump, or build with MSVC.
11. **Keyword-index RAM floor.** The FST must be resident and contiguous (0.05–0.15 GB [E]), and the size of the global-threshold index is not measured yet (E30e).
12. **Fusion and BM25 precision.** The weights w and c must be re-tuned, because asymmetric scores ≈ 0.8 × cosine. On-the-fly BM25 is approximate for the ≈15 % long records, since tf comes from the prefix only.
13. **Memory outside the budget.**
    - Python result objects: k = 500 with text = "full" produces MBs.
    - The 357 MB tokenizer parse peak at open.
    - Two archives during a hot swap.
14. **Previews look final.** The fast preset is much weaker (vector-only P@10 0.183 vs 0.229). Clients must check `reranked` / `degraded` before treating results as final.
plan.decisions_needed:
1. **Go-ahead.** On 2026-10-14 you asked to document the compact profile but not implement it yet. May we start Phase 0 (measurements) and Phase 1 (Python library on today's format)? Neither commits to a format.
2. **Final LM.** It must be fixed before the 5-day compression of all HN.
   - Option A: use lm-hn-70m as it is (trained on 1 % of HN).
   - Option B: first train it on 5 % (≈7 h on the iGPU), for an estimated −2–4 % of text (≈−60–110 MB).
3. **Vector bits.**
   - 256 bits: ≈5.45 GB, about today's quality on the sample.
   - 192 bits: ≈5.1 GB, −0.011 P@10 at top-200.
   - 384 bits, if E30d shows K must grow with corpus size.
   - Recommendation: decide after E30d; default 256.
4. **Default quality and deadline.**
   - balanced: ≈3.5–4.5 s cold, 6 s deadline.
   - precise: ≈7 s.
   - Is an anytime answer with `degraded=True` acceptable when the deadline hits?
5. **Keyword-only search.**
   - Accept that frequent terms are found only among vector candidates (recommended).
   - Or keep a frequent-term index for ≈+1.4–1.8 GB.
6. **Meaning of `ram`.**
   - Proposal: the process working set minus the baseline at open, excluding the OS file cache and returned Python objects. Commit can be ≈0.5 GB higher because of OpenVINO.
   - Should `ram` default to "2GB" or be a required argument?
7. **Embedder device and deployment hardware.**
   - On machines with the iGPU: GPU at ≥4 GB (faster cold queries, smaller cache) or always CPU?
   - Will every deployment have an Intel iGPU? GPU-less servers are ≈0.5–1 s slower on cold queries.
8. **OpenVINO runtime.**
   - Depend on the pip package (recommended; 247 MB outside the block).
   - Vendor the DLLs in the wheel (64–99 MB).
   - Long term: our own Rust encoder.
9. **Build toolchain.** May MSVC Build Tools be installed for wheel builds, or must everything use GNU + WinLibs?
10. **Disk use beyond the block.**
    - Default: nothing besides the block (recommended).
    - Optional, opt-in: a persistent warm-cache file (≈1 KB per warmed doc), idle background warming, and an OpenVINO compile cache (≈0.3 GB, cuts GPU startup by ≈3–10 s). Which of these are allowed?
11. **Block shape.**
    - 3 files: container + embed.xml + embed.bin (recommended).
    - A single file instead needs either a zero-copy OpenVINO weights path or a +272 MB transient copy at open.
12. **Lossless verification of the full build.**
    - Stratified 0.5 % sample (≈2.4 h) plus the check byte on every full decode (recommended).
    - Or a full decode of everything (≈20 days of CPU, in the background).
13. **`kids` order.** Store it (≈+50–100 MB), or keep the current documented exclusion?
14. **Smaller choices.**
    - Python 3.10+ abi3 only, no free-threaded build: OK?
    - HTTP on localhost without auth: OK?
    - Keep the legacy fast-profile reader (10.4 GB, ≈26 ms hot) for development and as an option? Recommended: yes.

issues.issue: The RAM cap is enforced on process WorkingSet minus a baseline taken at open(). In a shared Python process that number is not a ledger of hnz memory. Python result objects, which the plan says are excluded, are counted anyway. Host-app growth after open() and a second Archive during a hot swap land in the same number. Memory the host frees after open() hides hnz growth. The feedback loop then evicts caches and 'pauses admission until memory is back under the limit'. If the excess is not hnz cache (the host or OpenVINO grew, or a second archive is open), eviction cannot fix it. Every call then ends in BusyError after queue_timeout: an outage, not a degradation. Separately, buffered streaming at 2 GB or less leaves about 1-1.5 GB of vector codes in the OS standby cache. That memory is outside `ram` and the user is not told.
issues.fix: Enforce the cap on a ledger that hnz owns. Use the RAII reservations; take the Rust heap from a counting allocator or mimalloc stats; set the Opaque class from measured PeakWorkingSetSize/PrivateUsage deltas over tokenizer load plus a max-shape warm-up of every OpenVINO stream. Use the WS sampler only for stats() and one bounded correction of Opaque, and never gate admission on WS. Document that host memory and the OS file cache are outside `ram`, or use io=direct for streamed scans when codes are not resident. Also offer a simpler, stricter out-of-process mode: the Python package is a client of hnz.exe serve over localhost or a named pipe. There the process WS belongs to hnz alone, a Job object gives a kernel backstop, and a hot swap is a process restart.

issues.issue: The CPU embedder path cannot meet its stated cold-balanced latency of 3.8-4.8 s. That path is the default (ram="2GB") even on this iGPU machine, and the only path on GPU-less servers. The '≈50 docs/s' figure for batched CPU re-embedding is unmeasured. The only measured CPU document rate is 19.9 docs/s (E10: fp16, static 32x128, all 16 cores). E23's 2.5x int8 gain was batch-1 query latency, which is memory-bound; weight-only int8 does not speed up compute-bound batched GEMMs. Even at 50 docs/s on all cores, 115 re-embeddings (≈26-29 P-core-equivalent seconds) plus the 3.2 s, 8-thread LM decode (≈20-23) need at least 4 s on 6P+8E+2LPE with perfect overlap. With 20-30 docs/s and E17-style barrier stalls, 6-10 s is realistic (estimate). The 18-24 ms query-embedding figure was measured with the LATENCY hint, not with the planned INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS=4 / NUM_STREAMS=2. Finally, the device rule (GPU only at ram ≥ 4 GB) gives up 2-6 s of re-embedding to keep 0.55 GB of codes resident, which saves only about 0.2-0.4 s of stage 1.
issues.fix: Before freezing the presets, measure batched CPU document embedding (dynamic int8 vs fp16) while the LM is decoding. Make the planner use the iGPU whenever one is present and its floor fits, streaming codes instead. By the plan's own numbers that floor is ≈1.15 GB embedder + 0.46 + ≈0.13 pools ≈ 1.75 GB, so it fits at 2 GB. For CPU-only deployments either use K_v = 50 (E27a: 0.219 vs 0.225 at top-100) or publish about 6-10 s. Correct P4's CPU acceptance numbers accordingly.

issues.issue: Continuous batching without parking makes every LM-dependent latency depend on whatever cold queries are running. Step time grows with the number of active slots: ≈27.8 ms at 64 slots (64 / 2,300 tok/s, from E26 verify) versus ≈2.8 ms at 10 active (E17). Priority only orders admission; it does not shorten steps. While one balanced query is decoding: fast-preset snippets (≈66 tokens) take ≈1.8 s, against a claim of 0.35-0.6 s and a 2 s deadline. Every Title wave adds ≈0.4 s. text="full" and get() advance one token every ≈28 ms. Under sustained cold load a 1,000-token get() takes ≈28 s; the plan claims 0.2-0.6 s, which E26 measured on an idle decoder. The plan rejected D2's 'parking' as unnecessary, but parking is exactly what is needed, and here it costs nothing.
issues.fix: Batch::step(&active, …) already takes a subset of slots. A parked job keeps its exact-capacity KV and simply skips steps; no paging is involved. In the scheduler, cap the active set whenever Interactive or Fetch jobs are waiting (for example ≤16 slots, or a ≈5 ms step-time target). Park bulk Prefix and Background jobs, and reserve a share of steps for Fetch. Choose S from E30g's throughput AND per-token-latency curves. First remove the per-step allocations: the 12.8 MB logits Vec and the 64 x 400 KB `cum` Vecs in store.rs sample(). The current data show no throughput gain from a large S: ≈3,500 tok/s at 10 active vs ≈2,300 at 64, though on different workloads. So 48-64 slots mostly buy KV memory and latency.

issues.issue: Two lossless gaps. (a) The order of `kids` is still excluded even though the requirement is lossless, and the plan prices storing it at +50-100 MB. I measured it here: coding each kids list as a permutation of the children known from parent pointers costs Σlog2(c!) ≤ 0.11-0.13 B/item on 2010-06, 2015-06 and 2020-06. That is ≤ ≈6 MB for all of HN, plus a 'kids absent' flag (2024-01 has no kids at all) and exceptions for ids that do not match parent pointers. The derived `words` column should be declared out of scope. (b) The record check byte hashes only the record's own text, not its id or docnum. A pack bug that reorders or misplaces records therefore produces valid but wrong text that passes rec_check. The stratified 0.5% decode sample catches one misplaced 32-record group with only ≈15% probability (1 - 0.995^32).
issues.fix: Store kids as per-parent permutations, on by default, and measure the exceptions in P3. In pack and verify-block, add a 100% byte-level check that needs no decoding: for every HN id, the copied header, check byte and payload must equal that id's record in the per-period lm.bin. This takes minutes, not days. Keep the 0.5% decode sample to cover numerics.

issues.issue: The build order breaks the promise that one Rust function builds the prompts at build time and at query time (decision 6). P0 freezes P and starts the 2-3 day full prefix-embedding run, but `hnz prompts` / prompt.rs (doc_prompt + plain_prefix + the LM-token cut) only arrives in P3. Any later change to that function invalidates days of iGPU work. embed_prompts.py would also re-tokenize the prompt strings with the Python `tokenizers` package, whose version differs from the Rust crate 0.23. Finally, zstd-fallback records (≈0.01%, including every record over 2,000 tokens) need the LM tokenizer for the P-token cut, but that tokenizer is not loaded at query time.
issues.fix: Write prompt.rs in P0, cover it with golden tests and record a prompt_version in the manifest. Have `hnz prompts` emit Gemma token ids produced by the Rust tokenizer, and have embed_prompts.py feed those ids directly. Define the prefix of fallback records as a byte cut on a character boundary, applied identically at build and query time.

issues.issue: The stage-1 figure of 30-60 ms over 47M codes is unvalidated, and both the warm p50 (80-150 ms) and the fast preset depend on it. E14 (6.3 ms for 365k codes over 6 parallel 64K chunks) and E26 (4.1 ms hybrid for 629k docs over ≈11 chunks) imply up to ≈70-100 ns per doc per thread for the current loop (an upper bound that includes fixed costs). That means up to 0.4-0.6 s on 8 threads. Also, the stage-1 rayon pool (8 threads) + LM spin pool (8) + OpenVINO CPU (8) = 24 busy threads on 6P+8E+2LPE, which recreates E17's pathology (17.3 s vs 1.03 s per batch). E30g measures the LM only against OpenVINO on CPU, not against stage 1 or the iGPU. E18 showed both slowing down when the LM and the iGPU ran together (72 rec/s; 126-131 docs/s).
issues.fix: Make P2's synthetic 49M-code test a gate with an explicit target of about 5 ns per doc per thread: contiguous 32 B codes, unchecked AVX2 popcount, and a threshold test before any heap operation. Partition the cores with CPU Sets (LM on P-cores; stage 1 and OpenVINO on E-cores), or run stage-1 chunks on the spin pool between LM steps. Add LM + stage-1 and LM + iGPU contention runs to E30g.

issues.issue: E27a's result ('256 bits + top-200 ≈ no loss') does not test the planned search. bench_rescore.py ranked candidates by an exhaustive asymmetric score over all 611k docs, not by the planned pipeline (Hamming top-C1, then LUT). At 47M docs, thousands of codes tie at the C1-th Hamming distance (estimate ~8k per distance value). vecs.rs keeps the lowest docnums among ties (strict `ham < peek`, then a sort by (ham, doc)). That is a systematic cut against recent documents. The recall loss of the Hamming prefilter has never been measured at this scale either (E14: -0.7% at 365k). And only 384 sign dims are kept, so any fallback beyond 384 bits would need another 3-day embedding run.
issues.fix: Make E30d replay the exact pipeline: Hamming C1 with the real tie rule, inline filters, the keyword union, and prefix re-embeddings. Break ties by LUT score or by a deterministic hash(doc, query). Keep sign bits for 512-768 dims in the build scratch (+0.8-2.4 GB) so any width can be packed without re-embedding.

issues.issue: The documented hot swap contradicts 'one Archive per process', and process-wide resources were not designed for two archives. The GPU plugin keeps its memory after the model is dropped (session probe: 1.46 GB WS falls only to 1.15 GB), so each swap on GPU leaks about 1 GB. The LM SpinPool is a process-global OnceLock with a single job slot. Two DecodeServices overwrite each other's job there; the displaced submitter finishes its job alone, which is correct but E17-slow. Per-archive rayon pools double the stage-1 threads, and two WS-based budgets watch the same process number.
issues.fix: Make EmbedService (OpenVINO Core + compiled model) and the LM/DecodeService process-wide singletons, keyed by model hash and shared by all archives. A hot swap then only swaps data parts and ledger entries. Alternatively, forbid concurrent archives and swap snapshots by restarting the process, which fits the out-of-process mode.

issues.issue: A single warm-up at maximum shape does not capture OpenVINO's opaque memory. On CPU, dynamic shapes cache compiled primitives per distinct shape (CPU_RUNTIME_CACHE_CAPACITY defaults to 5000), and NUM_STREAMS=2 allocates intermediate buffers per stream, lazily. On GPU, each new shape triggers a kernel compile: a stall of hundreds of ms and memory that is never returned. Compilation also has transient peaks above the steady level. Static bucket IRs were chosen for the iGPU originally for this reason (E10, E13: 204 docs/s); dynamic int8 on GPU has not been measured.
issues.fix: Pad queries and documents to a fixed set of shapes, for example batch {1, 4, 16} x seq {32, 64, 128, 256}. At open, warm every (shape, stream) pair and cap CPU_RUNTIME_CACHE_CAPACITY at the number of shapes. Reserve the peak delta (PeakWorkingSetSize / PrivateUsage), not the steady WS. In P0, compare dynamic int8 against static fp16 buckets on GPU, in docs/s and memory, before choosing.

issues.issue: Determinism needs hardening now that the LM runs inside an arbitrary host process. The LM math assumes MXCSR = 0x1F80: round_even's MAGIC trick needs round-to-nearest, and denormal handling matters in softmax and attention. SpinPool::run also executes tasks on the submitting thread. Nothing asserts any of this. The text transform (htmlx transform/restore, to_lm/from_lm) is as load-bearing as MATH_VERSION but has no version. The Rust toolchain is not pinned. The canaries are ≤150 tokens, so long positions are never exercised.
issues.fix: Set and assert MXCSR on every LM thread and before each step, and fail loudly on a mismatch. Pin rustc with rust-toolchain.toml for both build and runtime and record it in the manifest. Add a transform_version. Add one ≈1,500-token canary that is decoded in the background after open.

issues.issue: Two claims overstate ranking determinism: 'cold and warm runs rank identically' and 'results are independent of RAM residency'. Re-embeddings differ by device (f32 activations on CPU vs f16 on GPU), and the device depends on `ram`. They also differ with bucket and batch composition, which depends on batcher timing under concurrency, so EmbI8 values near rounding boundaries can flip. The P2/P4 acceptance tests that require 'rankings identical' will therefore be flaky.
issues.fix: State the determinism guarantee per device. In tests, compare rankings with a score tolerance that allows near-ties. If exact reproducibility matters, make document embedding batch-invariant (fixed padding per bucket, kernels that do not depend on batch size).

issues.issue: Smaller correctness and API gaps: (a) The QueryCache would also store degraded (deadline-cut) rankings and keep serving them after the machine is idle again. (b) get_many / POST /items and query-string length have no caps, although decoded outputs and tokenization are hnz memory. (c) The on-the-fly 'exact' BM25 uses plain_prefix, which keeps a link's URL and drops its anchor text. The index used htmlx::to_plain, which keeps the anchor text and drops the href. So a rare-term hit can get tf = 0 after rescoring. (d) In keyword mode, 'a query term that appears in no document makes the result empty' contradicts today's OR semantics. (e) The whole crate is built with target-cpu=x86-64-v3, so an AVX2 guard inside _hnz.pyd can crash with an illegal instruction during module init. (f) E30c tunes (w, c) on the same 900 queries that P4 then uses for acceptance.
issues.fix: (a) Do not cache degraded results, or re-run the query when the machine is idle. (b) Cap ids per call (≤500) and query size (for example 4 KB), and charge outputs to the query's reservation. (c) Use one text function, derived from the LM text, for both the index build and rescoring. (d) Keep OR semantics. (e) Check IsProcessorFeaturePresent(PF_AVX2_INSTRUCTIONS_AVAILABLE) in __init__.py before importing _hnz. (f) Tune on one half of the queries and run acceptance on the other half.

issues.issue: The schedule is optimistic. P0/P5 assume LM compression (≈115 rec/s) and iGPU embedding (≈200 docs/s) overlap freely. The measured rates when they ran together were 72 rec/s and 126-131 docs/s (E18). That means about 7.5-8 days of machine time whether the two runs are sequential or parallel, not 5-6. Building per year also loses up to 10-12 h of work on a crash.
issues.fix: Plan for about 8 days. Build the LM text per month (pack regroups the payloads anyway) so resuming is finer-grained, and checkpoint the embeddings per month.

issues.issue: RAM above about 4 GB barely helps cold queries, which contradicts the user's expectation that 10 GB will be 'faster'. The 10 GB column reserves 5.4 GB of caches, but they fill at about 115 docs per cold query. Filling them takes about 50k cold queries (≈41 h at the 0.33 q/s ceiling), and they are lost on restart. Going from 4 GB to 10 GB saves milliseconds (author column, resident metadata), not seconds.
issues.fix: Tell the user this plainly. Let the planner leave RAM it cannot use unallocated. If 'more RAM = faster' matters, bring forward opt-in idle warming of the newest months (≈137k prefix docs per hour at 2,300 tok/s) and/or the opt-in warm file.

review.verdict:
Revise the plan before committing to the format. Phase 1 (the Python library on today's format) can start now.

**Verified as correct against the code and data:**
- KV cache costs 24,576 B per token and logits 196.5 KiB per slot (hidden 512, 6 layers, vocab 50,304; read from the lm-hn-70m header).
- Exact-capacity KV and mixing jobs from different queries in one batch keep the output bit-identical. `krow` slicing does not depend on capacity, and each slot's math is independent of the others.
- 2,300 tok/s comes from E26 verify: 29 rec/s x 79.4 tokens at 64 slots.
- ≈61 decode tokens per candidate holds. On 2015-06 I measured the top-100 256-bit candidates: mean min(ntok,130) = 61.2 and min(ntok,224) = 69.3, with no skew toward long docs. That gives ≈7.3-7.5k tokens, about 3.2 s per balanced query.
- HN ids and times are monotonic and months do not overlap (checked 2006-10 to 2007-04 and 2015-05 to 2015-07), so a global docnum with contiguous date ranges works.
- iGPU allocations do show up in the process working set and are not returned after the model is dropped (session probe).

**Blocking issues:**
1. The RAM cap measured as process WS minus a baseline can turn host-app growth into a permanent BusyError outage.
2. The CPU embedder path, which is the default at ram=2GB, is about 6-10 s per cold query, not 3.8-4.8 s. The device rule picks it even when an iGPU is available.
3. Continuous batching without parking makes get(), text="full" and fast-preset latency depend on whatever cold queries are running.

**Before the multi-day P0 runs:**
- Freeze prompt.rs, with golden tests and token-id output.
- Keep at least 512 sign dims.

**To be truly lossless:**
- Store the kids order; I measured it at ≤≈6 MB for all of HN.
- Add a 100% byte-level check of the pack.

**Simpler alternatives that would work:**
- Park jobs by leaving them out of the existing `active` subset passed to `Batch::step`.
- Use the GPU whenever one is present.
- Use a static ledger instead of WS feedback.
- Offer an out-of-process `hnz.exe` mode for strict RAM isolation and hot swap by restart.
